eng_text: Regarding the global financial situation, Zapatero continued by saying that "the financial system is a part of the economy, a crucial part.

eng_text: We have a year-long financial crisis, which has had its most acute moment in the past two months, and I think now the financial markets are beginning to recover."

text: I tērā wiki, i tauākītia e Naked News ka kaha whakapiki ia i tōna mana reo ā-ao ki te pūrongo i ngā kōrero o te wā, ki ngā pāhotanga hou e toru.
eng_text: Last week, Naked News announced that it would dramatically increase its international language mandate to news reporting, with three new broadcasts.

text: Kua oti kē te tuku rīpoata ki roto i te reo Ingarihi me te reo Hapanihi, kei te whakarewahia e ngā kaiwhakahaere o te ao whānui i ngā kaupapa reo Pāniora, Itāria me Korea hoki mō te pouaka whakaata, te ipurangi me ngā waea pūkoro.
eng_text: Already reporting in English and Japanese, the global organization is launching Spanish, Italian, and Korean-language programs, for television, the web, and mobile devices.

text: Te waimarie kāore au i ahatia, ēngari i kite au i tētahi kāpeka wetiweti i te wā i ngana ngā tāngata ki te pākaru i ngā wini kia puta atu.
eng_text: "Luckily nothing happened to me, but I saw a macabre scene, as people tried to break windows in order to get out.

text: I te patu ngā tāngata i ngā matapihi ki ngā tūru, engari kāore i taea ngā matapihi te whawhati.
eng_text: People were hitting the panes with chairs, but the windows were unbreakable.

text: "Kātahi anō ka pakaru tētahi o ngā matapihi, ā, kā tīmata rātou te puta atu mā te matapihi," te kōrero a te morehu a Franciszek Kowal.
eng_text: One of the panes finally broke, and they started to get out by the window," said survivor Franciszek Kowal.

text: Kei te whakaputa aho, wera hoki ngā whetū nā te pūngao ka hangaia i te whakakotahi (te kōmitimiti rānei) i ngā ngota hauwai hei hanga i ngā pūmotu taumaha ake.
eng_text: Stars give off light and heat because of the energy made when hydrogen atoms are merged (or fused) together to form heavier elements.

text: E ngana ana ngā kaimātai pūtaiao ki te hanga i tētahi momo pūrere e ōrite ana tōna whakaputa ngao.
eng_text: Scientists are working to create a reactor that can make energy in the same way.

text: Heoi anō, he raru uaua tēnei hei whakaoti, ā, ka haere ngā tini tau i mua i tā tātou kite i te hanganga o ngā whare hiko honokarihi.
eng_text: This, however, is a very hard problem to solve and will take many years before we see useful fusion reactors built.

text: Ka mānū te ngira maitai i runga ake o te wai nā te kaha o te mata.
eng_text: The steel needle floats on top of the water because of surface tension.

text: Ka hua mai te renarena mata nā te mea e kaha ana te whakamanea a ngā rāpoi ngota wai ki te mata o te wai tētahi ki tētahi, he nui ake i te whakamanea ki ngā rāpoi ngota hau ki runga rā.
eng_text: Surface tension happens because the water molecules at the surface of the water are strongly attracted to each other more than they are to the air molecules above them.

text: Nā ngā rāpoi ngota wai ka puta he kiri kore kitea ki te mata o te wai e tukuna ana i ngā mea pērā i te ngira ki te rere ki runga i te wai.
eng_text: The water molecules make an invisible skin on the water’s surface that allows things like the needle to float on top of the water.

text: Kei te mata o tētahi reti tio hou tētahi matarua me te pūaha kōpapa ki waenganui. Kei te whakaahei ngā taha e rua kia pai ake te piri ki te tiao, ahakoa kua tītahatia.
eng_text: The blade on a modern ice skate has a double edge with a concave hollow between them. The two edges allow for a better grasp of the ice, even when tilted.

text: Nā te mea kei te āhua ānau te taha whakararo o te mata, ka tītaha te mata ki tētahi taha, ki tērā atu taha rānei, ka ānau hoki te taha e pā ana ki te tio.
eng_text: Because the bottom of the blade is slightly curved, as the blade tilts to one side or the other, the edge which is in contact with the ice also curves.

text: Mā konā te kaireti e tahuri. Ki te tītaha ngā reti ki te taha matau, ka huri whakatematau te kaireti, ki te tītaha ngā reti ki te taha mauī, ka huri whakatemauī te kaireti.
eng_text: This causes the skater to turn. If the skates tilt to the right, the skater turns right, if the skates tilt to the left, the skater turns left.

text: Kia hoki ake ki te taumata ngoi i reira kē rātou, me tuku atu ngā ngoi tāpiri kua riro mai i te tūrama.
eng_text: To return to their previous energy level, they must get rid of the extra energy they got from the light.

text: Ka pēnei rātou mā te whakputa i tētahi korakora ririki o te aho e kīia ana he "pūaho".
eng_text: They do this by emitting a tiny particle of light called a "photon".

text: Ka karangatia tēnei mahinga e ngā kaipūtaiao te "stimulated emission of radiation" i te mea e hikohikongia ana ngā ngota e ngā raiti muramura, e puha ai te pūaho o te raiti, me te mea hoki he momo raiti te hihi.
eng_text: Scientists call this process "stimulated emission of radiation" because the atoms are stimulated by the bright light, causing the emission of a photon of light, and light is a type of radiation.

text: Ko te pikitia whai ake e whakaatu ana i ngā ngota e whakaputa ana i ngā rāpoi ngota. Ae mārika, he iti noa atu ngā rāpoi ngota ki ēnā kei te pikitia.
eng_text: The next picture shows the atoms emitting photons. Of course, in reality photons are a lot smaller than those in the picture.

text: He iti noa ake ngā pūaho i ngā mea e hanga ai i te ngota!
eng_text: Photons are even smaller than the stuff that makes up atoms!

text: Whai muri i ngā tini hāora o te mahi, ka pakarū te kaka o te rama, ā, ka kore anō te rama e mahi.
eng_text: After hundreds of hours of operation the filament in the bulb eventually burns out and the light bulb no longer works.

text: Kātahi me whakakī te pūrama. Me āta tūpato i te wā e whakakapi ana i te pūrama.
eng_text: The light bulb then needs replacing. It is necessary to be careful in replacing the light bulb.

text: Me mātu weto i te kōhao rama me wete rānei i te taura hiko.
eng_text: First, the switch for the light fixture needs to be turned off or the cable disconnected.

text: I te mea ko te hiko e rere nei ki te papa e noho nei te wāhanga konganuku o te umanga, ka tūmeke tō hiko me ka pā atu koe ki roto o te umanga, ki te turanga whakarewa rānei o te pēra i te wā kei roto paku toni i te kōhao.
eng_text: This is because electricity flowing into the socket where the metallic part of bulb sits can give you a severe electric shock if you touch the inside of the socket or the metal base of the bulb while it is still partly in the socket.

text: Ko te okana nui o te pūnaha rerenga ko te manawa, e whakarere nei i te toto.
eng_text: The major organ of the circulatory system is the heart, which pumps the blood.

text: Ka rere atu te toto i te manawa ki ngā pū e kīia ana he ia-tuku, ā, ka hoki mai ki te manawa ki ngā pū e kīia ana he ia-auraki. Ko ngā pū iti rawa e kīia ana he ngongo rauangi.
eng_text: Blood goes away from the heart in tubes called arteries and comes back to the heart in tubes called veins. The smallest tubes are called capillaries.

text: Ko te niho o te Triceratop kua taea te kuru i ngā rau me ngā peka rākau tīno kaha, me ngā akaaka anō hoki.
eng_text: A triceratops' teeth would have been able to crush not only leaves but even very tough branches and roots.

text: kei te whakapono ētahi kaipūtaiao i kai ngā Triceratops i ngā cycads, arā ko tētahi momo tipu i kitea whānuitia i te wā Cretaceous.
eng_text: Some scientists think Triceratops ate cycads, which are a type of plant that was common in the Cretaceous.

text: He rite te āhua o ēnei rākau ki ngā nīkau iti, he karauna koi, me ngā rau taratara.
eng_text: These plants look like a small palm tree with a crown of sharp, spiky leaves.

text: Kua taea e te Triceratops te whakamahi i tana ngutu kaha kia mahura i ngā rau i mua i te kāinga o te tīwai.
eng_text: A Triceratops could have used its strong beak to strip off the leaves before eating the trunk.

text: E tohe ana ētahi kaimātai pūtaiao he nui ngā paitini a ngā hua nei, nā reira kāore nei pea i kainga e te mokoweri, ahakoa i ēnei rā ka kainga e te māngere me ētahi atu kararehe pēnei i te kākā (he nuri kāwai nā ngā mokoweri) ka taea te kai rau paitini, hua rākau hoki.
eng_text: Other scientists argue that these plants are very poisonous so it is unlikely that any dinosaur ate them, even though today the sloth and other animals like the parrot (a descendant of the dinosaurs) can eat poisonous leaves or fruit.

text: Ka pēhea tā Io kume-ā-papa e kukume i ahau? Ki te tū koe i runga i te mata o Io kua iti ake tō taumaha tēnā i tō taumaha ki runga o Papatūānuku.
eng_text: How would Io's gravity pull on me? If you stood on the surface of Io, you would weigh less than you do on Earth.

text: Ko te tangata he 200 pauna (90kg) tana te taumaha ki te Ao nei ka 36 pauna (16kg) tana taumaha ki runga i Io. Nō reira kāore e pērā rawa te kaha o te aukume e tō nei i a koe.
eng_text: A person who weighs 200 pounds (90kg) on Earth would weigh about 36 pounds (16kg) on Io. So the gravity, of course, pulls less on you.

text: Kāore he kiri tō te rā e rite ana ki tō tātou Ao e taea ai koe te tū. Hangaia mai ai te rā i te haurehu, i te ahi me te parahama.
eng_text: The Sun doesn't have a crust like the Earth that you can stand on. The whole Sun is made out of gases, fire, and plasma.

text: Ka iti iho te haurehu i a koe ka toro atu ai mai i te pokapū o te Rā.
eng_text: The gas becomes thinner as you go farther from the center of the Sun.

text: Ko te wāhanga ki waho e kitea ana e tātou i te tiro atu ki te Rā e kīia ana ko te photosphere, ko tōna tikanga ko te "pōro o te tūrama".
eng_text: The outer-part we see when we look at the Sun is called the photosphere, which means "ball of light".

text: Tata ki te toru mano tau i muri, i te tau 1610, i whakamahia e te kaimātai whetū nō Itāria a Galileo Galilei tētahi karu whātata kia kite he mata ā Kōpū, pērā i ā te marama.
eng_text: About three thousand years later, in 1610, Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei used a telescope to observe that Venus has phases, just as the moon does.

text: Ka tū mai ngā mata nā te mea ko te taha o Meremere (o te Marama rānei) e tūrama ana ko te taha e aro ana ki te Rā anake. I tautoko ngā mata o Meremere i te ariā o Copernicus ka rere ngā aorangi huri noa i te Rā.
eng_text: Phases happen because only the side of Venus (or of the Moon) facing the Sun is lighted. The phases of Venus supported the theory of Copernicus that the planets go around the Sun.

text: Kātahi, ētahi tau whai muri mai i te 1639, nā tētahi kaimātai whetū ko Jeremiah Horrocks tōna ingoa, i kite i tētahi whakawhitinga o Kōpū.
eng_text: Then, a few years later in 1639, an English astronomer named Jeremiah Horrocks observed a transit of Venus.

text: I mau te rongo taketake ki roto Ingarangi i muri mai i te raupatutanga o te Danelaw.
eng_text: England had experienced a long period of peace after the reconquest of the Danelaw.

text: Heoi anō i te tau 991 i arohia a Elthred e tētahi kahupapa Viking rahi ake i tētahi mai i tō Guthrum te kotahi rautau i muri iho.
eng_text: However in 991 Ethelred was faced with a Viking fleet larger than any since Guthrum's a century earlier.

text: Nā Olaf Trygvasson tēnei kāhui i ārahi, he uri nō Nōwini e hiahi ana ki te whakahoki mai i te mana o tōna whenua i te iwi o Denmark.
eng_text: This fleet was led by Olaf Trygvasson, a Norwegian with ambitions to reclaim his country from Danish domination.

text: Whai muri i ngā heke ope tauā tīmatanga, i āhei a Ethelred te whakaae ki ngā whakaritenga ki a Olaf, i hoki ia ki Nōwei kia ngana ki te whiwhi i tana kīngitanga, he rangirua te eke.
eng_text: After initial military setbacks, Ethelred was able to agree to terms with Olaf, who returned to Norway to try to gain his kingdom with mixed success.

text: Ko te Hangeul te ororeta e rongonui ana i roto i ōna whakamahinga o ia rā. I hangaia mai te ororeta i te tau 1444 i te wā o te heipūtanga a Kīngi Sejong (1418-1450).
eng_text: Hangeul is the only purposely invented alphabet in popular daily use. The alphabet was invented in 1444 during the reign of King Sejong (1418 – 1450).

text: Ko King Sejong te kīngi tuawhā o te Joseon Dynasty, ā, ko ia tētahi o ngā mea tino whakarangatiratia.
eng_text: King Sejong was the fourth king of the Joseon Dynasty and is one of the most highly regarded.

text: I tapa tūturu ia i te arapū Hanguel ki Hunmin Jeongeum, ko tōna tikanga ko "ngā oro tika mō te whakaako i te tangata".
eng_text: He originally named the Hangeul alphabet Hunmin Jeongeum, which means "the correct sounds for the instruction of the people".

text: He maha ngā ariā mō te ahunga mai o te Sanskrit. Ko tētahi o ēnei e pā ana ki te hekenga Aryan mai i te uru ki Īnia nā rātou te reo i kawe mai.
eng_text: There are many theories to how Sanskrit came into existence. One of them is about an Aryan migration from the west into India who brought their language with them.

text: He reo tāukiuki te Sanskrit, ko tōna rite ko te reo Rātini e kōrerotia ana ki Ūropi.
eng_text: Sanskrit is an ancient language and is comparable to the Latin language spoken in Europe.

text: I tuhia te pukapuka tuatahi o te ao ki te reo Sanskrit. Whai muri mai i te whakahiatotanga o Upanishards, e memeha noa iho a Sanskrit i ngā mahi nahanaha.
eng_text: The earliest known book in the world was written in Sanskrit. After the compilation of Upanishads, Sanskrit just faded due to hierarchy.

text: He reo pīroiroi, he reo hōhonu te reo Sanskrit, ā, ko ia hoki te reo taketake o ngā tini reo Īniana o nāianei, pērā i te reo Rātini hei reo taketake mō ngā reo Ūropi pērā i te reo Wīwi me te reo Pāniora.
eng_text: Sanskrit is a very complex and rich language, which has served to be the source for many modern Indian languages, just like Latin is the source for European languages like French and Spanish.

text: I te mutunga o te pakanga mō Wīwī, i tīmata a Tiamani te whakarite kia eke i te motu o Peretānia.
eng_text: With the battle for France over, Germany began to get ready to invade the island of Britain.

text: I whakaingoatia munangia e Tiamani te āki ki te "Operation Sealion". Ko te nuinga o ngā taputapu whawhai o Piritania i ngaro i te wehenga o Dunkirk, nō reira i āhua ngoikera ai te tauā.
eng_text: Germany code-named the attack “Operation Sealion”. Most of the British Army's heavy weapons and supplies had been lost when it evacuated from Dunkirk, so the army was fairly weak.

text: Engari i kaha tonu ake te Royal Navy i te German Navy ("Kriegsmarine", ā, kua taea te turaturaki i te kāhui whakaeke ka tukuna mai i te English Channel ahakoa tēhea.
eng_text: But the Royal Navy was still much stronger than the German Navy (“Kriegsmarine”) and could have destroyed any invasion fleet sent across the English Channel.

text: Heoi anō, he iti noa ngā kaipuke Royal Navy tata ki ngā ara eke e tinga ana nā te mataku a ngā atimira ka totohu pea i te eke ā-hau Tiamani.
eng_text: However, very few Royal Navy ships were based near the likely invasion routes as the admirals were afraid they would be sunk by German air attack.

text: Me tīmata mai i ngā whāinga a Itāria. I mua atu, ko Itāria ka noho hei "teina" ki a Tiamana me Hapāna.
eng_text: Let's start with an explanation about Italy's plans. Italy was mainly the "little brother" of Germany and Japan.

text: Kāore i pēra rawa te kaha o te ope taua me te ope moana, ahakoa kātahi anō rātou ka hanga i ngā kaipuke e whā i mua tonu mai i te pakanga.
eng_text: It had a weaker army and a weaker navy, although they had just built four new ships right before the beginning of the war.

text: Ko ngā whāinga matua a Itaria ko ō Awherika whenua. Kia riro i ēnā whenua me hanga he papa whakarere mō ngā hōia kia pai ai te rere i te moana Mediterranean me te tomo i a Awherika.
eng_text: Italy's main goals were African countries. To capture those countries, they would need to have a troop launching pad, so as troops could sail across the Mediterranean Sea and invade Africa.

text: Mō tēnā, i peia atu e rātou ngā hanganga me ngākaipuke nō Peretānia ki Īhipa. Hāunga aua mahi, tōna tikanga me kaua ngā waka tauā a Itari e paku aha atu.
eng_text: For that, they had to get rid of British bases and ships in Egypt. Besides those actions, Italy's battleships were not supposed to do anything else.

text: Nā, mō Hapani ināianei. He motu whenua a Hapani pēnei tonu hoki i a Peretānia.
eng_text: Now for Japan. Japan was an island country, just like Britain.

text: Ko te waka whakatakere he kaipuke kua hoahoatia kia haere ki rō wai, kia noho ki reira mō tētahi wā roa.
eng_text: Submarines are ships designed to travel underwater, and remain there for an extended amount of time.

text: I hautū ngā waka whakatakere i te Pakanga Tuatahi/Tuarua o te Ao. I ērā rā he pōturi ngā waka nei, ā, kāore nei e tino whānui te pūhitanga o ngā pū.
eng_text: Submarines were used in World War I and World War II. Back then they were very slow and had a very limited shooting range.

text: I te tīmatanga o te pakanga i haere rātou mā te moana, engari nā te hanga mai o te irirangi whakaata, ka mutu, he hāngai tika hoki, ka mate ngā waka whakatakere te ruku ki raro i te moana kia kore ai hoki e kitea.
eng_text: In the beginning of the war they mostly travelled on top of the sea, but as radar began developing and becoming more accurate the submarines were forced to go under water to avoid being seen.

text: I kīa ai ngā waka tōpū o Tiamana he U-Boat. He tohunga ngā tiamana ki te whakatere i ō rātou waka tōpū ki te moana.
eng_text: German submarines were called U-Boats. The Germans were very good at navigating and operating their submarines.

text: I runga i tō rātou angitu ki ngā waka whakatakere, whai muri i te pakanga kāore i te tino whakaponohia kia whai ngā Tiamani i te maha o ērā.
eng_text: Because of their success with submarines, after the war Germans aren't trusted to have many of them.

text: Āe! Ko Kingi Tutankhamun, e kīa nei ko "King Tut" ko te "kingi tama" rānei tētahi o ngā kingi tawhito o Īhipa e rongonui tonu ana i ēnei rā nei.
eng_text: Yes! King Tutankhamun, sometimes referred to as "King Tut" or "The Boy King", is one of the most well known ancient Egyptian kings in modern times.

text: Waihoki, kāore ia i whai whakaarotia hei tino hira i ngā wā o nehe, ā, kāore ia i tuhia ki te nuinga o ngā rārangi kīngi tawhito.
eng_text: Interestingly, he was not considered to be very important in ancient times and was not recorded on most ancient king lists.

text: Heoi, nā tāna hura i tēnei toma i te tau 1922 i rongonui ai ia. Inā kē he maha ngā toma o mua kua pāhuahuatia, i waiho noatia tēnei toma.
eng_text: However, the discovery of his tomb in 1922 made him a celebrity. While many tombs of the past were robbed, this tomb was left virtually undisturbed.

text: Ko te nuinga o ngā taonga i nehua ki a Tutankhamun kua pai te whakauka, tae atu ki ngā tini mano taonga kua hangaia ki ngā mētara tongarerewa me ngā kōhatu ongeonge.
eng_text: Most of the items buried with Tutankhamun have been well preserved, including thousands of artefacts made from precious metals and rare stones.

text: Nā te auahatanga mai o ngā wīra ngā hāriata Assyrian i māmā ake, i tere ake, i pai ake te whakarite kia rere atu i ngā hōia, i ētahi atu hāriata hoki.
eng_text: The invention of spoke wheels made Assyrian chariots lighter, faster, and better prepared to outrun soldiers and other chariots.

text: Ka āhei ngā kōpere mai i ā rātou kōpere whakamate te ngotongoto i te kākahu ārai o ngā hōia hoariri. Tata ki te 1000 B.C., i whakatūria e te hunga Assyrian te ope hōia eke hōiho tuatahi.
eng_text: Arrows from their deadly crossbows could penetrate the armor of rival soldiers. About 1000 B.C., the Assyrians introduced the first cavalry.

text: Ko te karawhiri he tauā e pakanga ana mā runga hōiho. Kāore anō te nohonga hōiho i hangaia, nō reira i pakanga te karawhiri Assyrian mā runga i te tuarā ake o ō rātou hōiho.
eng_text: A cavalry is an army that fights on horseback. The saddle had not yet been invented, so the Assyrian cavalry fought on the bare backs of their horses.

text: Kei te mōhio tātou ki ngā kaitōrangapū, ki ngā kaipūtaiao, ki ngā ringa toi maha o ngā Kiriki. Ākuanei pea ko te tangata tino rongonui mō tēnei ahurea ko Homer, te kairotarota kāpō e kōrerotia ana, nāna i tito ngā mounga e rua o ngā tuhinga Kiriki: arā ko ngā rotarota Lliad me te Odyssey.
eng_text: We know many Greek politicians, scientists, and artists. Possibly the most known person of this culture is Homer, the legendary blind poet, who composed two masterpieces of Greek literature: the poems Iliad and Odyssey.

text: He kaitito rongonui tonu a Sophocles me Aristophanes, ā, kei runga noa atu ō rāua titonga i roto i te ao tuhituhi.
eng_text: Sophocles and Aristophanes are still popular playwrights and their plays are considered to be among the greatest works of world literature.

text: Ko ētahi atu kaipāngarau rongonui Kariki ko Pythagoras, e mōhiotia ana mō tōna ariā rongonui e pā ana ki ngā hononga o ngā tahataha o ngā tapatoru hāngai.
eng_text: Another famous Greek is a mathematician Pythagoras, mostly known for his famous theorem about relations of the sides of right triangles.

text: E rerekē ana ngā matapae mō te nui o te hunga kōrero Hindi. E matapaetia ana koinei tētahi o ngā tino reo puta noa i te ao.
eng_text: There are varying estimates for how many people speak Hindi. It is estimated to be between the second and fourth most commonly spoken language in the world.

text: E rerekē ana te tau o ngā kaikōrero ūkaipō i runga i te tatau, kāore rānei i ngā mita tino tata te hononga.
eng_text: The number of native speakers varies depending on whether or not very closely related dialects are counted.

text: Mai i te 340 miriona ki te 500 miriona ngā whakatau tata o ngā kaikōrero, ā, tae atu ki te 800 miriona tāngata ka mārama ki te reo.
eng_text: Estimates range from 340 million to 500 million speakers, and as many as 800 million people can understand the language.

text: He rite te Hindi me te Urdu ki te taha wete reo heoi he rerekē te taha tuhinga; I roto i te reo ōpaki ka mārama ngā kaikōrero i te nuinga o te wā ō rātou ake reo.
eng_text: Hindi and Urdu are similar in vocabulary but different in script; in everyday conversations, speakers of both languages can usually understand each other.

text: Nō te rautau 15 i noho ai a Estonia ki te Raki i raro i te maru o Tiamana.
eng_text: Around the 15th century, northern Estonia was under great cultural influence of Germany.

text: I hiahia ētahi monaki Tiamani kia tuku i te Atua kia tata ake ki ngā iwi taketake, nō reira i hanga rātou i te reo ā-kiko o Etōnia.
eng_text: Some German monks wanted to bring God closer to the native people, so they invented the Estonian literal language.

text: I hangaia ki te arapū o Tiamani, ā, i āpitihia atu tētahi reta, te "Ō/ō".
eng_text: It was based on the German alphabet and one character "Õ/õ" was added.

text: I te wehenga o te wā, he tini ngā kupu Tiamani i whakakotahingia. Ko te timatanga tēnei o te hīnātore.
eng_text: As time passed, many words that were borrowed from German coalesced. This was the beginning of enlightenment.

text: I ngā wā o nehe, ko te toto kikorangi ka tonoa kotahitia ki te kura pakanga whai muri i te mutunga o te kura.
eng_text: Traditionally, the heir to the throne would go straight into the military after finishing school.

text: Heoi, a Tiare i kura ki te whare wānanga ki te Kārihi o Trinity, ki Kemureti i ako ai ia i te mātauranga tangata me te mātai whaipara tangata, me muri ake te Hītori kia riro i te 2:2 (he tohu pae rua taumata tuarua).
eng_text: However, Charles went to university at Trinity College, Cambridge where he studied Anthropology and Archaeology, and later History, earning a 2:2 (a lower second class degree).

text: Ko Charles te mema tuatahi o te Whānau Kīngi o Peretānia kia whakawhiwhia ki tētahi tohu paetahi.
eng_text: Charles was the first member of the British Royal Family to be awarded a degree.

text: 3% o te whenua ko Tāke ki Ūropa (ko Thace ki te rāwhiti, ko Rumelia ki te kūrae o Balkan rānei)
eng_text: European Turkey (eastern Thrace or Rumelia in the Balkan peninsula) includes 3% of the country.

text: Ko te rohe o Tākei he nui ake i te 1,600 kiromita (1,000 māero) te roa, ā, he 800 km (500 māero) te whānui, ā, he tapawhā te āhua.
eng_text: The territory of Turkey is more than 1,600 kilometres (1,000 mi) long and 800 km (500 mi) wide, with a roughly rectangular shape.

text: Ko te rohe o Tākei, kei roto hoki ngā roto, e noho ana ki te 783,562 koromita pūrua (300,948 maero pūrua), mai i tērā kei te tonga mā uru o Āhia te 755,688 kiromita pūrua (291,773 maero pūrua), ā, kei Ūropi te 23,764 kiromita pūrua (9,174 maero pūrua).
eng_text: Turkey's area, including lakes, occupies 783,562 square kilometres (300,948 sq mi), of which 755,688 square kilometres (291,773 sq mi) are in south west Asia and 23,764 square kilometres (9,174 sq mi) in Europe.

text: Kei te 37 o ngā whenua nui katoa o te ao te rohe o Turkey, ā, he pēnei pea te nui i a Metropolitan Wīwi me te Kingitanga Kotahitanga kua hono.
eng_text: Turkey's area makes it the world's 37th-largest country, and is about the size of Metropolitan France and the United Kingdom combined.

text: Kei te karapotia a Tākei e ngā moana ki ngā taha e toru: te Aegean Sea ki te uru, te Black Sea ki te raki, me te Mediterranean Sea ki te raki.
eng_text: Turkey is encircled by seas on three sides: the Aegean Sea to the west, the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

text: He roa tā Luxembourg hītori, engari ko tōna mana motuhake ka hoki noa atu ki te tau 1839.
eng_text: Luxembourg has a long history but its independence dates from 1839.

text: Ko ētahi wāhi o nāianei o Belgium he wāhanga o mua o Luxembourg ēngari i Belgianngia whai muri i ngā tau 1830 o te hurihanga nui a Belgian.
eng_text: Present-day parts of Belgium were part of Luxembourg in the past but became Belgian after the 1830s Belgian Revolution.

text: Mai rā anō kua ngana a Luxembourg kia noho tonu hei whenua ngū engari i nohoia e Tiamani i te Pakanga Tuatahi o te Ao me te Pakanga Tuarua o te Ao.
eng_text: Luxembourg has always tried to remain a neutral country but it was occupied in both World War I and World War II by Germany.

text: I te tau 1957 i tū a Luxembourg hei mema whakatū o te whakahaere e mōhiotia ana ināianei hei Te Kotahitanga o Ūropi.
eng_text: In 1957 Luxembourg became a founding member of the organization which is today known as the European Union.

text: Ko te Drukgyal Dzong tētahi pā, kua huri kāweka, he whare noho, whare karakia nō te hunga Buddhist ki te wāhi ō-runga o te Paro District (ki Phondey Village).
eng_text: The Drukgyal Dzong is a ruined fortress and Buddhist monastery in the upper part of the Paro District (in Phondey Village).

text: Ko te kōrero e kī ana i te 1649 i hanga a Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel i te pā nui hei whakamaumahara i tana wikitoria ki ngā hoiā Mongol o Tibetan.
eng_text: It is said that in 1649, Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyel created the fortress to commemorate his victory against the Tibetan-Mongol forces.

text: I te tau 1951, i mahue noa mai ētahi tāonga i te weranga nui ki Drukgyal Dzong, pērā ki te whakaahua mō Zhabdrung.
eng_text: In 1951, a fire caused for only some of the relics of the Drukgyal Dzong to remain, such as the image of Zhabdrung Ngawang Namgyal.

text: Whai muri i te ahi, i tiakina, i haumarutia te pā, nā ka noho hei tētahi o ngā whakamanea manawa reka rawa o Bhutan.
eng_text: After the fire, the fortress was preserved and protected, remaining to be one of Bhutan's most sensational attractions.

text: I te wā o te rautau 18 i kitea e Cambodia kua kōpēa ia ki waenganui i ngā hoa noho tata taikaha, i a Thailand me Vietnam.
eng_text: During the 18th century Cambodia found itself squeezed between two powerful neighbors, Thailand and Vietnam.

text: I eke ngā Thais i Kamapōtia i ētahi wā i te rautau 18, ā, i te tau 1772 i whakahotu rātou i Phnom Phen.
eng_text: The Thais invaded Cambodia several times in the 18th century and in 1772 they destroyed Phnom Phen.

text: I ngā tau whakamutunga o te rautau 18 i eke hoki te hunga Witināma i Kamapōtia.
eng_text: In the last years of the 18th century the Vietnamese also invaded Cambodia.

text: Tekau mā waru paehēneti o te hunga nō Wenehūera kāore he mahi a rātou, ā, ko te nuinga o te hunga he mahi ā rātou e mahi i roto i te ohaoha ōpaki.
eng_text: Eighteen percent of Venezuelans are unemployed, and most of those who are employed work in the informal economy.

text: He rua hautoru Venezuela e mahi āna kei roto i te wāhanga ratonga, tata ki te koata ka mahi ki roto i te ahumahi, ā, he haurima kei roto i te ahuwhenua.
eng_text: Two thirds of Venezuelans who work do so in the service sector, nearly a quarter work in industry and a fifth work in agriculture.

text: Ko tētahi ahumahi hira ki te hunga nō Wenehūera ko te hinu, arā he kaituku atu ki tāwahi te whenua rā, ahakoa kotahi ōrau anake kei te mahi ki te ahumahi hinu.
eng_text: An important industry for Venezuelans is oil, where the country is a net exporter, even though only one percent work in the oil industry.

text: Tata ki te tīmatanga o te tū motuhake o te whenua, nā ngā pukenga o Singapore Botanic Gardens i āwhina ki te huri i te motu ki tetahi Garden City takiwā pārū.
eng_text: Early in the nation's independence, Singapore Botanic Gardens' expertise helped to transform the island into a tropical Garden City.

text: I te tau 1981, i kōwhiritia a Vanda Miss Joaquim, arā ko tētahi momorua māika, hei pua ā-motu o te whenua.
eng_text: In 1981, Vanda Miss Joaquim, an orchid hybrid, was chosen as the nation's national flower.

text: Ia tau i te wāhanga o te Oketopa ka haere atu te rahinga tata ki te 1.5 miriona kaiota ki ngā papatairite o te tonga, e whakawhiti nei i te Mara River mai i ngā puke ki te raki mō ngā ua.
eng_text: Every year around October nearly 1.5 million herbivores travel towards the southern plains, crossing the Mara River, from the northern hills for the rains.

text: Ana ka hoki ki te raki mā te taha uru, he whakawhiti anō i te awa o Mara, kia oti rā anō ngā marangai i te marama o Aperira.
eng_text: And then back to the north through the west, once again crossing the Mara river, after the rains in around April.

text: Kei te takiwā Serengeti te Serengeti National Park, te Ngorongoro Conservation Area me te Maswa Game Reserve ki Tānahia, me te Maasai Mara National Reserve ki Kēnia.
eng_text: The Serengeti region contains the Serengeti National Park, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and Maswa Game Reserve in Tanzania and the Maasai Mara National Reserve in Kenya.

text: Ko te ako ki te hanga pāpaho whakawhitiwhiti me tikanga hou, tikanga tawhito hoki, me waia hoki ki te whakamahi i ngā taputapu kei ngā karaehe (whakatakoto kōrero, te etitā ā-oro, ā-kiriata, te tuku kōrero, aha atu).
eng_text: Learning to create interactive media requires conventional and traditional skills, as well as tools mastered in interactive classes (storyboarding, audio and video editing, story telling, etc.)

text: Ki te hoahoa pāhekoheko me tiro anō koe ki āu pōhēhē mō te whakaputanga pāpāho me te ako me pēhea e whakaaro auaha.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that you re-assess your assumptions about media production and learn to think in a non-linear ways.

text: Kei te hiahia te hoahoa pāhekoheko kia tūhono ai ngā waehanga o tētahi kaupapa tētahi ki tētahi, engari me mārama hoki hei tūtahi wehe kē.
eng_text: Interactive design requires that components of a project connect to each other, but also make sense as a separate entity.

text: Ko te taumahatanga o ngā arotahi whakatata ko te pīroiroi arotahi me te tau o ngā āhuatanga arotahi e hiahiatia ana hei whakatutuki i te whānuitanga o ngā whāroa arotahi he nui ake i tērā o ngā arotahi matua.
eng_text: The disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the focal complexity and number of lens elements required to achieve a range of focal lengths is much greater than for prime lenses.

text: E āhua tata ana tēnei ki te take iti kore nei i te mea ka teitei ake te kounga o ngā mahi a ngā kaihanganga mata mō ngā hanganga mata.
eng_text: This is becoming less of an issue as lens manufacturers achieve higher standards in lens production.

text: Mā tēnei ka āhei ngā karaehe topa mō ngā pikitia ki tētahi momo kounga e rite ana ki ērā karaehe e hōmiromiro ana.
eng_text: This has allowed zoom lenses to produce pictures of a quality comparable to that achieved by lenses with fixed focal length.

text: Ko tētahi ngoikore kē atu o ngā karaehe topa ko te kohanga nui (te tere) o te mata i te nuinga o te wā he iti ake.
eng_text: Another disadvantage of zoom lenses is that the maximum aperture (the speed) of the lens is usually lower.

text: Nā konā he uaua te whakamahi i ngā arotahi whakatata iti te utu ki ngā āhuahanga iti te aho kore kōwhā.
eng_text: This makes inexpensive zoom lenses hard to use in low-light conditions without a flash.

text: Ko tētahi o ngā raru e tino kitea ana ina ngana ana ki te whakahuri i tētahi kiriata ki te hanganga DVD ko te whakarahi aunoa.
eng_text: One of the most common problems when trying to convert a movie to DVD format is the overscan.

text: E hangaia ana te nuinga o ngā pouaka whakaata kia reka ai ki te iwi whānui.
eng_text: Most televisions are made in a way to please the general public.

text: I runga i taua take, kua tapahia ngā taha, ki runga, ki raro, ki ngā tahataha o ngā mea katoa ka kitea ki te pouaka whakaata.
eng_text: For that reason, everything you see on the TV had the borders cut, top, bottom and sides.

text: Ka pēnei kia whakarite ka kapi te whakaahua i te katoa o te mata. Ko te ingoa mō tēnā ko te panoni rahi whakaahua.
eng_text: This is made to ensure that the image covers the whole screen. That is called overscan.

text: He mea whakarapa, ina hanga koe i tētahi DVD, ka tapahia hoki pea ōna tahataha, ā, mehemea he tino tata ngā kupu tōraro tā te kiriata he tata rawa ki te taha whakararo, kāore e whakaaturia katoatia.
eng_text: Unfortunately, when you make a DVD, it's borders will most likely be cut too, and if the video had subtitles too close to the bottom, they won't be fully shown.

text: Kua roa te pākaha tūturu nō neherā e whakaawe ana i te whakaaro, ka whakaarohia he whakaahua o ngā whakataetae, ngā hākari, te hoahoatanga Arthurian anō hoki.
eng_text: The traditional medieval castle has long inspired the imagination, conjuring up images of jousts, banquets and Arthurian chivalry.

text: Ahakoa kei te tū ki roto i ngā whare pakaru kotahi mano tau te tawhito he māmā te tō mai ki te hinengaro ngā oro me ngā rongo o ngā pakanga i neherā, kia tata rongo i te tatangi pāua ki ngā kōhatu, me te rongo i te mataku e whanake haere ana i ngā rua poka.
eng_text: Even standing amidst thousand year-old ruins it is easy to bring to mind the sounds and smells of battles long gone, to almost hear the clatter of hooves on the cobbles and to smell the fear rising from the dungeon pits.

text: Engari kua hangaia tā tātou pōhewa ki te ao kikokiko? He aha i hangaia ngā whare kīngi i te tuatahi? I pēhea te hoahoa, te hanga?
eng_text: But is our imagination based on reality? Why were castles built in the first place? How were they designed and built?

text: E kaha kitea ana i aua wā rā, ko te whare ariki o Kirike Muxloe he whare pā tēnā i tētahi whare ariki tūturu nei.
eng_text: Typical for the period, Kirby Muxloe Castle is more of a fortified house than a true castle.

text: Kaore e tino roa ka kore ngā matapihi nunui me ōna pakitara e taea te karo i te tomokanga mai.
eng_text: Its large glazed windows and thin walls would not have been able to resist a determined attack for long.

text: I te tekau tau 1480, i te tīmatanga mai o tōna hanganga e Lord Hastings, he āhua maungārongo ki te whenua, ā, ka hiahiatia anake te whakawawao ki ngā rōpū iti o te hunga konihi e hāereere ana.
eng_text: In the 1480s, when its construction was begun by Lord Hastings, the country was relatively peaceful and defense was only required against small bands of roving marauders.

text: Ko te taurite o te mana ko tētahi pūnaha nā korā ngā whenua Ūropi i whai kia whakaū i te tino rangatiratanga ā-whenua o ngā whenua katoa o Ūropi.
eng_text: The balance of power was a system in which European nations sought to maintain the national sovereignty of all European states.

text: Ko te ariā kia whāia e te katoa o ngā whenua Ūropi kia aukati i te tū mana mai o tētahi whenua, ā, nō reira he rite tonu te panoni a ngā kāwanatanga ā-motu i ō rātou noho haumi kia ū tonu te noho taurite.
eng_text: The concept was that all European nations had to seek to prevent one nation from becoming powerful, and thus national governments often changed their alliances in order to maintain the balance.

text: Ko te War of Spanish Succession te pakanga tuatahi ko te take matua ko te taurite o te mana.
eng_text: The War of Spanish Succession marked the first war whose central issue was the balance of power.

text: He tohu tēnei o tētahi tīnitanga nunui, nā te mea kāore ngā mana Pākehā he pakanga hāhī tēnei. Me te aha, ko tēnei pakanga torutekau tau te pakanga whakamutunga e tohua ai he pakanga hāhī.
eng_text: This marked an important change, as European powers would no longer have the pretext of being religious wars. Thus, the Thirty Years' War would be the last war to be labeled a religious war.

text: I turakina te temepara o Artemis me Ephesus i te 21 o Hūrae, 356 BCE, he ahi tinihanga a Herostratus.
eng_text: The temple of Artemis at Ephesus was destroyed on July 21, 356 BCE in an act of arson committed by Herostratus.

text: E ai rā te paki, ko tana whakahihikotanga ko te rongonuitanga ahakoa te aha. I pukuriri mārika ngā Ephesians, ā, ka mea kia kauka rawa te ingoa o Herostratus' e tuhia.
eng_text: According to the story, his motivation was fame at any cost. The Ephesians, outraged, announced that Herostratus' name never be recorded.

text: I tuhia tēnā ingoa e te kaituhi nō Kariki, a Strabo, i mōhio ai tātou i ēnei rā. I turakina te temepara i te pō o te whānautanga mai o Alexandra the Great.
eng_text: The Greek historian Strabo later noted the name, which is how we know today. The temple was destroyed on the same night that Alexander the Great was born.

text: Ka hiahia utu te kīngi, a Alexandra, i te tūnga mai anō o te temepara, engari auare ake. Nō muri mai, ka mate a Alexandra, nāwai rā, ka tū mai anō te temepara i te tau 323 BCE.
eng_text: Alexander, as king, offered to pay to rebuild the temple, but his offer was denied. Later, after Alexander died, the temple was rebuilt in 323 BCE.

text: Kia mahara ake, me tau tō ringa i a koe e whakatangi ana i ngā oro - me ngana kia kaua e tino māro ngā nekenekenga kei ō ringa.
eng_text: Make sure your hand is as relaxed as possible while still hitting all the notes correctly - also try not to make much extraneous motion with your fingers.

text: Mā konei, kāore koe e tino ngenge. Kia maumahara kāore he take mō te pato i ngā patooro ki te tōpana nui mō te oro teitei ake pērā i tā te piano.
eng_text: This way, you will tire yourself out as little as possible. Remember there's no need to hit the keys with a lot of force for extra volume like on the piano.

text: Ki te kōriana, kia nui ake te kahaoro, ka whakamahia ngā pupuhi ki te pēhanga nui ake, te tere nui ake rānei.
eng_text: On the accordion, to get extra volume, you use the bellows with more pressure or speed.

text: Ko te wairuatanga ko te whai i te kotahitanga, te tuakiri, te māramatanga rānei ki tētahi ao, tētahi mana, tētahi pono wairua, Atua taioreore rānei.
eng_text: Mysticism is the pursuit of communion with, identity with, or conscious awareness of an ultimate reality, divinity, spiritual truth, or God.

text: Kei te rapu te kaiwhakapono i te wheako, i te mōhio ā-roto, i te māramatanga tōtika rānei ki te ao tūturu o ngā atua/te atua, ngā atua rānei.
eng_text: The believer seeks a direct experience, intuition, or insight into divine reality/the deity or dieties.

text: Kei te whai ngā apataki i ētahi wā o te ora, i ngā mahi rānei e takunetia ana kia whāngai i aua wheako.
eng_text: Followers pursue certain ways of living, or practices that are intended to nurture those experiences.

text: He rerekē pea ngā mahi tiramaka ki ngā whakapono a ngā Hāhi nā te tōna whaiwhai marika i te hōhonutanga me te taumata o te whakaaro, mātua rā hoki ko ēra e āio ana, e aronui ana, e hīkaka ana te āhua.
eng_text: Mysticism can be distinguished from other forms of religious belief and worship by its emphasis on the direct personal experience of a unique state of consciousness, particularly those of a peaceful, insightful, blissful, or even ecstatic character.

text: Ko Sikhism tētahi hāhi nō te paparahi āpiti Īnia. I ahu mai i te takiwā Punjab i te rautau 15 mai i tētahi whakawehenga hāhi ki roto i te hāhi Hinitū.
eng_text: Sikhism is a religion from the Indian sub-continent. It originated in the Punjab region during the 15th century from a sectarian split within the Hindu tradition.

text: Ki te hunga Sikh ko tō rātou hāhi he hāhi kē atu i te hāhi Hinitū, ahakoa kei te mihi rātou ki ōna pakiaka, me ōna tikanga Hinitū.
eng_text: Sikhs consider their faith to be a separate religion from Hinduism though they acknowledge its Hindu roots and traditions.

text: Ki tā te Sikh ko te Hāhi Gurmat, ki te reo Punjabi ko te "way of the guru." Ko te guru te tūāpapa o ngā Hāhi Inia katoa, engari ki tā te Hāhi Sikh he whāinga nui kei reira i hua mai ai ngā mātāpono o te Sikh.
eng_text: Sikhs call their religion Gurmat, which is Punjabi for "way of the guru". The guru is a fundamental aspect of all Indian religions but in Sikhism has taken on an importance that forms the core of Sikh beliefs.

text: I whakatūria te hāhi i te rautau 15 e Guru Nanak (1469-1539). E iwa ngā wānanga i whai i ana tapuwae.
eng_text: The religion was founded in the 15th century by Guru Nanak (1469–1539). There followed in succession a further nine gurus.

text: Heoi, i te marama o Hūne i te tau 1956 i whakamātautia ngā kī taurangi a Kruschev i te wā ko ngā whana i Pōrana, i reira ngā kaimahi e porotēhi nei mō te itinga kai me te whakaheke utu ka huri ki tētahi porotēhi hei whakahē whānui i te Communism kē.
eng_text: However, in June 1956, Krushchev's promises were put to the test when riots in Poland, where workers were protesting against food shortages and wage cuts, turned into a general protest against Communism.

text: Ahakoa i te mutunga, i tukuna e Krushchev ngā taika hei whakahoki i te noho tau, i tuku ia ki ētahi hiahia ohaoha, ā, i whakaae ia ki te kopou i te Wladyslaw Gomulka rorotu hei pirimia hou.
eng_text: Although in the end, Krushchev sent in tanks to restore order, he did give way to some economic demands and agreed to appoint the popular Wladyslaw Gomulka as the new prime minister.

text: Ko te Indus Valley Civilization ko tētahi nōhanga Bronze Age ki te tuawhenua Īnia ki te raki mā uru e whai wāhi ana te nuinga o Pakitāne o nāianei me ētahi takiwā ki Īnia ki te raki mā uru me Āwhekenetāna ki te raki mā rāwhiti.
eng_text: The Indus Valley Civilization was a Bronze Age civilisation in the northwest Indian subcontinent encompassing most of modern-day Pakistan and some regions in northwest India and northeast Afghanistan.

text: I puāwai te wāhi noho rā ki ngā hāpua o te Indus River nō reira tōna ingoa.
eng_text: The civilisation flourished in the basins of the Indus River wherefore it derives its name.

text: Ahakoa te whakapae a ētahi pukenga nā te noho o te hapori rā ki ngā riu o te Sarasvati River kua maroke ināianei, me kī ka tika ko te Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, ā, ko ētahi e kī ana ko te Harappan Civilization mō Harappa, te tuatahi o ōna wāhi kia keria i te tekau tau 1920.
eng_text: Although some scholars speculate that since the civilisation also existed in the basins of the now dried up Sarasvati River, it should be aptly called the Indus-Sarasvati Civilization, while some call it the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first of its sites to be excavated in the 1920s.

text: Nā te āhuatanga mārō a Tū o te emapara Rōma i tautoko ake ai te whanaketanga o te rongoā.
eng_text: The militaristic nature of the Roman empire aided in the development of medical advances.

text: I tīmatahia te taritari i ngā tākuta e Emperor Augustus, ā, ka tū rātou hei Roman Medical Corps tuatahi mō te whakamahi ki te rerenga mai o ngā pakanga.
eng_text: Doctors began to be recruited by Emperor Augustus and even formed the first Roman Medical Corps for use in the aftermath of battles.

text: I ngā tākuta poka te mātauranga mo ngā rongoā whakamoe huhua tae atu ki te rehunanu kua unuhia mai i ngā kākano papi me te scopolamine mai i te kākano herbane.
eng_text: Surgeons had knowledge of various sedatives including morphine from extracts of poppy seeds and scopolamine from herbane seeds.

text: I tīno mōhio rātou me pēhea e tapa ai kia ora ai ngā tūroro mai i te gangrene me te tourniquet me ngā clamp arterial hei whakatū i te rere o te toto.
eng_text: They became proficient at amputation to save patients from gangrene as well as tourniquets and arterial clamps to stem blood flow.

text: I roto i ngā tini rautau i tatū te emepara Rōma ki ngā rawa nunui i roto i te wāhanga rongoā, ā, nā rātou i mōhio ai tātou ki ngā tini mātauranga o te wā nei.
eng_text: Over multiple centuries, the Roman empire led to great gains in the field of medicine and formed much of the knowledge we know today.

text: Ko Pureland origami ko te origami me te here ka taea anake te kotahi te numi i te wā kotahi, kāore i te whakaaetia ngā numi pīroiroi ake pērā i ngā numi angamate, ā he wāhi waingohia kei te katoa o ngā numi.
eng_text: Pureland origami is origami with the restriction that only one fold may be done at a time, more complex folds like reverse folds are not allowed, and all folds have straightforward locations.

text: I whanaketia e John Smith i ngā tau 1970 hei āwhina i ngā kaipōkai torehuruhuru, i ērā rānei he iti noa ngā pūkenga nekeneke.
eng_text: It was developed by John Smith in the 1970s to help inexperienced folders or those with limited motor skills.

text: Ka ako ngā tamariki i te kitenga o ngā momo tāngata me ngā whakaaro horapa o te momo tangata i roto i tana ohinga, ā, ka whakatūkino ēnei kitenga i te whanonga.
eng_text: Children develop an awareness of race and racial stereotypes quite young and these racial stereotypes affect behavior.

text: Hei tauira, ko te hunga tamariki e tautohungia ana ki te iwi tokoiti e takahia ana i te korenga i pai i te kura i te nuinga o te wā ka mahi pai i te kura i te wā e mōhio ai mō te takahitanga o tana iwi.
eng_text: For instance, children who identify with a racial minority that is stereotyped as not doing well in school tend to not do well in school once they learn about the stereotype associated with their race.

text: Ko MySpace te whārangi tuatoru te rorotu e whakamahingia ana ki Ngā Whenua Tōpū o Amerika, ā, e 54 miriona ngā pūkete i tēnei wā nei.
eng_text: MySpace is the third most popular website used in the United States and has 54 million profiles currently.

text: Kua nui ngā tirohanga o te whārangi ipurangi nei, mō te taha hoki ki te ako.
eng_text: These websites have gotten a lot of attention, especially in the education setting.

text: He pāinga tō ēnei whārangi ipurangi, mō te taha ki te whakarite i ngā whārangi akomanga e tāea ai te whakauru i ngā ataata, ngā rangitaki, ngā whakaahua me ētahi kē atu mea hoki.
eng_text: There are positive aspects to these websites, which include, being able to easily setup a class page which can include blogs, videos, photos, and other features.

text: He māmā te tomo mai ki tēnei whārangi mā te whakarato noa i tētahi whārangi paetukutuku e māma ai te maumahara me te patopato mā ngā ākonga he raru ōna ki te whakamahi i te papatuhi rorohiko, ki te tuhituhi hoki rānei.
eng_text: This page can easily be accessed by providing just one web address, which makes it easy to remember and easy to type in for students who may have trouble using the keyboard or with spelling.

text: Ka taea te whakarite ki tāu i hiahia ai kia ngāwari ai te pānui, me te iti me te rahi rānei o te kara i wawatangia ai.
eng_text: It can be customized to make it easy to read and also with as much or little color as desired.

text: Ko te Attention Deficit Disorder "he āhuatanga o te roro ko te mea tautohu matua ko te takitoru o ngā tohumate arā ko te manawa rere, te manawarau, me te manawarahi, te ngoi tuwhene rānei".
eng_text: Attention Deficit Disorder "is a neurological syndrome whose classic defining triad of symptoms including impulsivity, distractibility, and hyperactivity or excess energy".

text: Ehara noa i te ako hauātanga, he ninipa ki te ako; "he 3 ki te 5 paeheneti o ngā tamariki ka pāngia, akuanei ko tōna 2 miriona o ā Amerika tamariki".
eng_text: It is not a learning disability, it is a learning disorder; it "affects 3 to 5 percent of all children, perhaps as many as 2 million American children".

text: Mō ngā tamariki whai ADD he uaua ki a rātou te aro ki ngā mahi kura, engari ka aro pū kē ki ngā mahi e pārekareka ana, pērā ki te tākaro kēmu, te mātaki pouaka whakaata rānei, te tuhi rerenga kōrero rānei kāore i te whai i ngā tikanga wetereo.
eng_text: Children with ADD have a hard time focusing on things like school work, but they can concentrate on things they enjoy doing like playing games or watching their favorite cartoons or writing sentences without punctuation.

text: He kaha tonu te hapa a ēnei tamariki, i te mea "e uru ana rātou ki ngā whanonga mōrearea, te whawhai me te wero i te mana" kia whakahihiko i ō rātou roro, i te mea e kore ō rātou roro e hihiko i ngā mea o ia rā.
eng_text: These children tend to get into a lot of trouble, because they "engage in risky behaviors, get into fights, and challenge authority" in order to stimulate their brain, since their brain can not be stimulated by normal methods.

text: Ka raru tēnei mea te whanaungatanga i te ADD i te mea kāore ētahi atu o ngā tamariki i te tino mārama he aha i rerekē ai taua tamaiti rā i ōna pūmanawa, ōna āhuatanga tuhi hoki.
eng_text: ADD affects relationships with other peers because other children can not understand why they act the way that they do or why they spell they way they do or that their maturity level is different.

text: I te wā i tīni ai te āheinga ki te whiwhi mātauranga me te ako i roto i tētahi āhuatanga kua whakahuatia ake i tīni hoki te terenga pūtaketanga o te whiwhi mātauranga.
eng_text: As the ability to obtain knowledge and to learn changed in such a way as mentioned above the base rate at which knowledge was obtained changed.

text: I rerekē te huarahi ki te nanao kōrero. I mutu kau noa te pēhitanga i roto i te mahara o te tangata kotahi, ēngari te āheinga ki te mahara ki ngā kupu i nui ake te aronga.
eng_text: The approach to obtaining information was different. No longer did pressure reside within individual recall, but the ability to recall text became more of a focus.

text: Ko te ngako, nā te Renaissance tētahi panoni hira ki te aronga ki te ako, me te hōrapa o te mātauranga.
eng_text: In essence, the Renaissance made a significant change in the approach to learning and the dissemination of knowledge.

text: Kāore e pēnei i ngā paraimete kē atu, kāore ngā homonids e whakamahi i ī rātou ringa ināianei ki te tima rerewē, kia hiki taumaha, ki tārere rānei i ngā rākau.
eng_text: Unlike other primates, hominids no longer use their hands in locomotion or bearing weight or swinging through the trees.

text: He rite tahi te rahinga o te ringa me te waewae o te Chimpanzee, e ataata nei ko te whakamahinga o te ringa hei kawe i te taumaha mō te hīkoi i ngā matimati.
eng_text: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: He poto iho te ringa tangata i te waewae, me ngā phalanges tōtika ake.
eng_text: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Ko ngā kōiwi mātātoko ringaringa e rua miriona ki te toru miriona tau te pakeke e whakaatu nei i te rerekētanga o te ringa mai i te rokomōhini ki te rāwekenga.
eng_text: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Kei te whakapono ētahi ko te pāngia e ngā tini moemoeā mārama ka whakaritea horihoritia ka pērā rawa te rite tonu ka pau pea te hau.
eng_text: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Ko te take matua mō tēnei āhuatanga ko te hua o ngā moemoeā mārama e whakaroa ana i te roanga o te wā i waenga i ngā āhuatanga REM.
eng_text: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: I runga i te hekenga iho o ngā REM ia pō, ko tēnei āhua ka tino pāngia koe e te moe tūturu, ka whakarauoratia tō tinana, ka iti iho ngā wā ka pā kia raru ai.
eng_text: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: E pērā ana te pau o te hau i tāu oho ake ia rua tekau, toru tekau meneti rānei me te mātakitaki i te pouaka whakaata.
eng_text: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: Ko ngā putanga e ai ki te nui o ngā wā ka ngana tōu roro kia moemoeā māramarama i ia pō.
eng_text: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Kāore i pai ngā hua mō ngā Itariana i Awherika ki te raki, mai anō i te timatanga. I roto katoa i te wiki o te taunga pakanga a Itaria i te Hūne te 10, 1940, i horo i a Piritania te 11 te pā Capuzzo i Libya.
eng_text: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Ki tētahi manukāwhaki ki te rāwhiti o Bardia, i mau i a Peretānia te Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief nō Itāria, a General Lastucci.
eng_text: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Nō te 28 o Hune, nā ngā pū i Tobruk i mate ai a Marshal Italo Balbo, te Kāwana-Tianara mō Rīpia, te pik tūranga hoki ki te whare o Mussolini.
eng_text: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Mō te marea katoa te hākinakina nei, te mahi taiepa, mai i ngā tauira e whai ana i tēnei mahi ki te Whare Wānanga tāe noa ki ngā tohunga kei te whakataetae Taumāhekeheke o te Ao.
eng_text: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: Kei te mātua tākarotia tēnei hākinakina ki te takotoranga takirua, arā ko tētahi fencer e whawhai ana ki tētahi atu.
eng_text: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Ko te korowha tētahi kēmu ka whakamahia e ngā kaitākaro ngā haupōro hei patu pōro ki ngā rua.
eng_text: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Tekau mā waru ngā kōhao ia kēmu, ka tīmata mai i te kōhao tuatahi, ka mutu i te kōhao tekau mā waru.
eng_text: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Ko te kaitākaro ka iti rawa āna tarawete, āna tiu ki te haupōro rānei, ki te whakaoti i te autaki ka toa.
eng_text: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Ka tākina te kēmu ki runga i te whenua, ā, he pōtehe ake te otaota kei te kōhao, ko te kākariki te ingoa.
eng_text: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Tērā pea ko te momo noa rawa o te mahi tāpoi ko tērā e whakaarohia ana e te tangata mō te hāereere: Tāpoi ā-rēhia.
eng_text: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: Koinei tā te tangata haere ki tētahi wāhi he tino rerekē i ā rātou mahi o ia rā hei whakatā, hei ngahau.
eng_text: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: Ko ngā moana, ko ngā papa whakangahau me ngā whenua noho puni ka muiatia rawatia e te hunga tūruhi.
eng_text: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Mehemea ko te whāinga o te toronga ki tētahi wāhi ko te whai mōhio e pā ana ki tana hītori, ki tana ahurea, kei te mōhiotia tēnei momo tāpoi hei tāpoi ahurea.
eng_text: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Ka toro atu pea ngā tūruhi ki ngā tohu whenua rerekē ki tētahi whenua ake, ka kōwhiri rānei rātou ki te arotahi ki te rohe kotahi.
eng_text: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Ko te kairaupatu, i tāna kitenga i ēnei mahi, e karanga ana kia whakakahangia tōna tauā.
eng_text: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: I roto i ngā ope tauā e whakapakari ana i ngā tūranga o mua ko ngā hapū hōia New Hampshire tuatahi, tuatoru hoki o ngā tāne e 200, ki raro i a Colonel John Stark rāua ko Colonel James Reed (ā muri ake ka tū rāua tahi hei Tianara).
eng_text: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: I tū atu ā Stark tāngata ki te pahiko o te pito raki o te tūnga o te Colonist.
eng_text: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: I te kōara a te tai timu i tētahi āputa ki te taha o te Mystic River ki te raki mā rāwhiti o te raenga kūiti, ka tere tā rātou whakaroa ake i te taiapa ki tētahi pātū kōhatu poto ki te raki ka mutu ki te taha o te wai ki tētahi tahuna paku.
eng_text: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: I whakatū a Gridley, a Stark rānei i tētahi pou tata ki te 100 putu (30 m) ki mua i te taiapa me te tohu kia kaua tētahi e pū i mua i te whakawhiti a ngā mea auau i a ia.
eng_text: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: I whakawhirinaki te mahere a Amerika ki te tuku i ngā ekenga ruruku mai i ngā wāhi e toru rerekē.
eng_text: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: Ka tohua e Tianara John Cadwalder he ara autaki ki te puku tonu o ngā hoia o Ingarangi, ki Bordentown kia kore ai e riro anō i ā rātou he rawa.
eng_text: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: Ka ārahina e General James Ewing te 700 marīhia whakawhiti i te awa ki Trenton Ferry, ka mau i te piriti ki te Assunpink Creek me te aukati i ngā ope hoariri i te pakiha atu.
eng_text: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: Ka whakawhiti te ope whakaekenga matua o ngā tāne e 2,400 i te awa e iwa maero ki te raki o Trenton, kātahi ka whakawehea ki ngā rōpū e rua, ko tētahi ki raro i a Greene, ko tētahi ki raro i a Sullivan, hei whakarewa i tētahi ekenga i mua i te ata hāpara.
eng_text: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: I runga i te panoni atu i te omanga hauwhā maero ki te haurua, ka iti iho te hiranga o te tere, ka noho mātua waiwai te manawa piharau.
eng_text: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Ka tika tō tātou taumata-tuatahi hāwhe-mira, he tāne e āhei te pīti i te rua miniti, kāore e kore he mōhio ki te tere, heoi me ngaki te manawanui i ngā raru katoa.
eng_text: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: Ko ngā oma roa hei te wā o te takurua me te mahi pītakataka mō runga ake o te tinana, koinei ngā huarahi pai ki te whakatika mō ngā wā o te oma.
eng_text: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: E kore te tangata e tohunga i tētahi mahi mā te tika o te kai anake, engari he pai mō te oranga tinana o te hunga rangatahi.
eng_text: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: Mā te mau tonu ki te hauora tika, mā te parakatihi i ngā tikanga inu wai tika me te mārama ki ngā āhuatanga rerekē o te whakakaha tinana e pai ake ai te whakangungu a te kaiaka me te āheinga kia pārekareka ake ai te hākinakina.
eng_text: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: He iti noa te utu o te oma tawhiti, heoi, he nui ngā heitara mō ngā taputapu iti nei ka whakamahia mō tēnei mahi.
eng_text: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: Ka hokona ngā putanga ina hiahiatia ana, ēngari kāore te nuinga e tino pā ki te mahi.
eng_text: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: Ka whakaaro ake ētahi kaiaka he pai ake rātou ki tētahi taputapu ahakoa kāore he hua tika ka kitea.
eng_text: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: E whai whakaarotia ana te ngota hei tētahi o ngā mea pūtake ka hanga i ngā matū katoa.
eng_text: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: He mea tino pīroiroi ia, e ai ki tētahi tauira Bohr kua whakamāmātia, ko ia tētahi karihi pū, e āmiohia ana e ngā irahiko, e āhua rite ana ki te āmio a ngā aorangi i te rā - tirohia Hoahoa 1.1.
eng_text: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: E rua ngā pūtūmua o te karihi - ngā iramoe me ngā iraoho.
eng_text: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: He whana hiko tōrunga tō te iraoho, ā, karekau he whana tō te iramoe. He tōraro te whana hiko iriiho.
eng_text: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Hei Tiro ki te parurenga, i te tuatahi me tiro koe ki te wāhi kia whakarite ka haumaru koe.
eng_text: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: Me mataara koe ki te takotoranga o te parurenga i tō kātata atu ki a ia, me ngā tohu mōrearea pea.
eng_text: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: Ki te whara koe i a koe e ngana ana ki te āwhina, ka kino ake pea i runga i tāu āwhina.
eng_text: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: E ai ki te rangahau, ko tēnei mea te pouri, te hopo me te whakaaro kino ngā hononga i waenganui i te mamae me te hauātanga mō ērā e mate tuara ana.
eng_text: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: Ko ngā putanga noa o te whakaaro kikino, kāore te whakamomori te wehi hoki i heipū mō ngā wiki i whakaritea mō ngā akomanga PA.
eng_text: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: Ko te hunga e whai wāhi ana ki te oi auau ka nui ake te tautoko ka hiahiatia e pā ana ki te tirohanga kino o te mamae me te whakawehe i ngā rerekētanga o te mamae me te manawarau wā-roa i te nekehanga ā-tinana noa.
eng_text: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: Ko te kitenga, ko te pūkenga kia kite rānei e whirinaki ana ki ngā whēkau rongo pūnaha kitenga, ki ngā karu rānei rānei.
eng_text: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: He rahi ngā momo kōiriiritanga o te karu, mō te taha ki te pīroiroi e hāngai ana ai ki ngā hiahia o te rauropi.
eng_text: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: He rerekē ngā āheinga o ngā hanganga rerekē, ā, he hūkokikoki ki ngā roanga-ngaru rerekē, ā, he rerekē te tika a tētahi ki tētahi, me te mea hoki me rerekē ngā mahinga kia mārama ai ki te āhua o te tāuru me ngā nama rerekē kia pai rawa te mahinga.
eng_text: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: Ko te taupori ko te kohinga koiora o tētahi ake momo ki roto tonu i tētahi takiwā ā-takotoranga papa e tautuhia ana.
eng_text: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: Ina ōrite tonu te katoa o ngā takitahi ki tētahi taupori e ai ki tētahi āhuatanga ake e kitea ana kei te mōhiotia hei āhuatanga kotahi.
eng_text: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Ka kite ana i tētahi momo a te tangata e kitea whānuitia ana, he iranga tūātinitini tēnā.
eng_text: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: Ka hīkoi ka whakawhānau hoki ngā koroni pōpokorua i ngā mata rerekē hoki.
eng_text: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: I te wā o te tipi whenua, ka hīkoikoi ngā hōia pōpokorua i te pō ka tū ai ki te noho tōpuni i te awatea.
eng_text: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Ka tīmata te huinga i tētahi wā tipiwhenua ina heke haere te kai e wātea ana. I tēnei wā, ka hangaia e te huinga ngā kōhanga taupua ka panonitia ia rā.
eng_text: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: Ko ia o ēnei ekenga, hīkoinga tipiwhenua rānei, he āhua 17 rā te roa.
eng_text: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: He aha nei te pūtau (cell)? I ahu mai te kupu cell mai i te kupu Rātini "cella", ko tōna tikanga ko "rūma iti", ā, i titoa tuatahitia e tētahi kaikaruwhakarahi i tana kite i te hanga o te puru.
eng_text: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Ko te pūtau te waehanga pūtake o ngā mea ora katoa, ā, kua hangaia ngā koiora katoa i te pūtau kotahi, neke atu rānei.
eng_text: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Ka pērā rawa te pūtaketake me te hira o ngā pūtau ki te ora, inā koa, e kīia nuitia ana ko "ngā poraka hanga o te ora".
eng_text: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Kei te ū tonu te pūnaha ioio ki te taurite mā te tuku i ngā karere io puta noa i te tinana kia haere tonu te rere o te toto, ka ukiuki anō hoki.
eng_text: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Ka pērā rawa te tere o te tuku i ēnei karere io puta noa i te tinana ka āwhinatia kia noho haumaru te tinana i tētahi whakatuma torohū.
eng_text: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Ka patu te āhiowhio i tētahi wāhi iti noa nei i ngā āwha kino, engari ka turakina te katoa e whakapōrearea ana i a ia.
eng_text: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Ka hūtia ngā rākau e te āwhawhiowhio, ka tīhae i ngā whare teitei, ka porowhiua hoki ngā motuka ki te rangi. Neke atu i te toru hāora ngā āwhawhiowhio kaha rawa atu e rērere ana.
eng_text: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Kei ēnei āwhā rahi rawa ngā hau tae atu ki te 480 km/h (133 m/s); 300m/h).
eng_text: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Kua hangaia, kua whakamahia hoki e te tangata ngā arotahi mō te whakarahi mō te tini mano tau.
eng_text: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

eng_text: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: E rua ngā māwhatu kei ēnei kau mātata e tawhiti, e tata mai rānei he taputapu ki a koe.
eng_text: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: Ēnei mea te apo me te matapiko, he āhuatanga e kore nei e taea te karo. Inā rā, i ngā wā e hora ana ngā painga, ka nui ake ngā painga mēnā ko te tokoiti e matapiko nei ka ora i ēnei painga.
eng_text: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

eng_text: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Tokomaha ngā tāngata ka pōhewa i te wā ka taea e te tangata te hāereere ki tētahi atu whetū me te torohē i ētahi atu ao, ka whai whakaarohia e ētahi tāngata he aha kei waho rā kei te whakapono ētahi he tautangata, he koiora anō kei te noho pea kei tētahi atu aorangi.
eng_text: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Heoi anō, mehemea ka hua mai tēnei kāore e hua mai i roto i te wā tata nei. Kei te pērā te horahora o ngā whetū he tini tiriona māero i waenganui i ngā whetū he "kiritata" rātou.
eng_text: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Akuanei i tētahi rā ka tū ō mokopuna i runga ake i tētahi ao manene e whakaaro ana mō ana tūpuna onamata?
eng_text: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: E hangaia ana ngā kararehe ki ngā tini pūtau. Ka kai rātou i ngā mea, ā, ka nakunaku i aua mea ki roto. Ka taea e te nuinga o ngā kararehe te nuku.
eng_text: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Kei ngā kararehe anake he roro (ahakoa kāore i te katoa o ngā kararehe; hei tauira, kāore he roro tō ngā pūkarukaru).
eng_text: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Ka kitea ngā kararehe ki ngā wahi katoa o te ao. Ka keri rātou i te papa, ka kaukau i te moana, ka rere hoki i te rangi.
eng_text: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Ko te ira te mea pāpaku rawa me te wāhanga whakatika o te rauropi (mea) ora.
eng_text: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Kua ahu mai te kupu pūtau i te kupu cella nō te reo Rātini ko tōna tikanga ko te rūma paku.
eng_text: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Ki te tiro koe ki ngā koiora ki raro i tētahi karu whakarahi,ka kitea e koe kua hangaia ki ngā tapawhā ōrite, ki ngā pōro iti rānei.
eng_text: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Nā Robert Hooke, tētahi kaimātai koiora nō Ingarangi, i kite ngā tapawhā ōrite paku ki te puru ki tētahi karu whakarahi.
eng_text: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: He rūma te āhua. Ko ia te tangata tuatahi ki te kite i ngā pūtau mate
eng_text: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Ka taea ngā pūmotu me ngā pūhui te neke mai i tētahi teiti ki tētahi atu, ā, e kore e tīni.
eng_text: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: He rite ngā haurehu o te hauota i tēnā o te hauota wai. Ko te hanga wai he mātotoru ake heoi he rite ngā rāpoi ngota.
eng_text: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Ko tētahi atu tauira ko te wai. Kua hangaia te pūhui wai ki ngā ngota hauwai e rua, me te ngota hāora kotahi.
eng_text: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: He ōrite te hanga rāpoi ngota he ahakoa he haurehu, he wē, he totoka rānei.
eng_text: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Heoi anō kei tīni te āhuatanga ā-kiko, ko te āhuatanga o te matū ka rite tonu.
eng_text: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Ko te wā ko tētahi mea e karapoti ana i a tātou, ā, kei te pā ki ngā mea katoa e mahi ana tātou, heoi anō he uaua te mārama.
eng_text: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Kua rangahaua te wā e ngā hāhi, e ngā kai rapunga whakaaro, me ngā mātanga o te pūtaiao mō ngā tau manomano.
eng_text: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: E mōhio ana tātou ko te wā he whakaraupapatanga kaupapa nō anamata, nō inamata, nō ōnamata anō hoki.
eng_text: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Mā te wā hoki e whakataurite ai tātou i te roanga o ngā mahinga.
eng_text: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: E taea e koe te kite ake i te hipanga o te wā mā te āta titiro ki te tōaitanga o tetahi mahi hurihuri. Ko tētahi mahi hurihuri ko tētahi mahi he auau te puta mai anō.
eng_text: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Ko ngā rorohiko i tēnei wā kei te whakamahia hei raweke i ngā whakaahua, i ngā kiriata anō hoki.
eng_text: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Ka taea te hanga ki ngā rorohiko ngā whakaari marutuna, ā, kei te piki haere te whakamahi i tēnei momo whakaari ki te pouaka whakaata, ki ngā kiriata anō hoki.
eng_text: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: He nui ngā wā ka rīkoatatia te puoro mā ngā rorohiko mātanga hei whakarite, hei whenumi tahi hoki i ngā oro.
eng_text: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Mō te wā roa, i te rautau 19 me te rautau 20, e whakaponotia ana ko te iwi tuatahi ki Aotearoa ko te iwi Māori, i aruaru ai rātou te manu nui e kīa ana ko te Moa.
eng_text: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Kātahi ka whakatū te ariā i te whakaaro i heke mai te hunga Māori i Poronīhia ki tētahi Kahupapa Nui, ā, ka tango i Aotearoa mai i ngā Moriori, me te whakatū i tētahi papori ahuwhenua.
eng_text: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Heoi anō, e marohi ana ngā taunakitanga hou ko te Moriori ko tētahi rōpū Māori nō te tuawhenua i heke atu i Aotearoa ki Rēkohu, me te whakawhanake i tō rātou ake ahurea motuhake, maungārongo.
eng_text: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: He iwi atu anō kei Rēkohu, ko te iwi Māori tēnei i haere mai i Aotearoa.
eng_text: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: I whakaingoatia rātou ko te Moriori, ā, i tini ngā whawhai, i te mutunga atu ka ngaro te Moriori.
eng_text: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: I āwhina ngā tāngata takitahi kua whai wāhi mai mō ngā tini tekau tau i a mātou ki te whakaute i ō mātou kaha, i ō mātou mea kohara, i te wā tonu e aromatawai ana i ngā taumahatanga, i ngā hinganga anō hoki pea.
eng_text: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: I te whakarongo ki ngā takitahi e whakaputa ana i ā rātou kōrero ā-takitahi, ā-whānau, ā-whakahaere hoki, ka whiwhi mātou i ngā māramatanga kahurangi ki te wā kua hipa, me ētahi o ngā tāngata i whakaaweawe mō te pai, te kino rānei te ahurea o te whakahaere.
eng_text: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Ahakoa te māramatanga ki tana hitori kāore i te rite ki te mōhiotanga o te ahurea, heoi ka āwhina i te tangata kia mōhio ai kihea rātou taka ai i roto i te hītori o te whakahaeretanga.
eng_text: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Ina arotake ana i ngā mea angitu, me te whai mōhio ki ngā mea hinga, ka hōhonu ake te kitea e ngā takitahi, e te hunga katoa e uru mai ana ngā uara, te whāinga, me ngā aronga matua o te rōpū whakahaere.
