eng_text: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: I tēnei wā, mā te maumahara ki ngā mahinga o mua a ngā whanonga rakahinonga me ngā angitu i hua mai, i āwhina i ngā tāngata kia noho tuwhera ki ngā panoni hou me te aronga hou mā te whare karakia o tērā wāhi.
eng_text: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Nā ngā kōrero angitu pēnei i heke haere ngā mataku mō te panoni, waihoki ka hangaia ngā aronga pai ki te panoni mō te wā e heke mai ana.
eng_text: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: He tikanga whakaoti rapanga ngā mahere whakaaroaro pūtahitanga e whakakotahi ana i ngā ariā, i ngā mātai rerekē hei rapu otinga.
eng_text: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Ko te aronga o tēnei momo whakaaro ko te tere, te whakakaupapa, me te tika, ā, ko te tautuhi i ngā meka, te whakahāngai anō i ngā tikanga o nāianei, te kohi mōhiohio.
eng_text: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Ko te mea nui o tēnei taumata whakaaro: kotahi noa te whakautu tika. E rua ngā whakautu ka whiriwhiria, ko te mea tika me te mea hē.
eng_text: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Ēnei whakaaro e hāngai ana ki ētahi kaupapa pūtaiao, tikanga arataki rānei.
eng_text: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Ko te hunga e pēnei nei ō rātou whakaaro he whakaaro whakakaupapa ōna, e taea nei te maumahara ki ngā tauira, te whakatika hapa me te mahi i ngā whakamātautau pūtaiao.
eng_text: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Ko te tangata te momo tino iho pumanawa rawa i te mōhio ki ngā whakaaro o ētahi atu.
eng_text: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: I runga i tēnā e pai ana tā tātou matapae i te kite, i te takune, i te whakapono, i te mōhio, i te hiahia rānei o tāngata kē atu.
eng_text: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: I roto i ēnei āheinga, he mea taketake te mārama ki te takunetanga o ētahi atu. Mā korā tātou e āhei ai te whakatau i ngā rangirua o ngā mahi ā-tinana.
eng_text: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Hei tauira, ki te kite koe i tētahi e pākaru ana i tētahi matapihi waka, ka whakaaro pea koe kei te ngana ia ki te tāhae i te waka o tētahi uakoau.
eng_text: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: Me rerekē te whakawā i a ia mēnā kua ngaro i a ia āna kī waka, ā, ko tōna ake waka tērā e ngana ana ia te maoho.
eng_text: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: E hāngai ana te MRI ki te kaupapa ahupūngao e kīa ana ko te karihi aukume whāorooro, i tūhuratia e Felix Bloch (i te mahi ki Te Whare Wānanga o Stanford) me Edward Purcell (nō Te Whare Wānanga o Harvard) i ngā tau 1930.
eng_text: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: I roto i tēnei tōiriiri, ko ngā whaitua autō me ngā hihi irirangi e whakaputangia ai ngā whakapua reo irirangi iti nei e ngā ngota.
eng_text: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: I te tau 1970, i hurangia e te tākuta rongoā me te kairangahau pūtaiao, e Raymond Damadian te paparahi mō te whakamahinga o te whakaahuatanga pākuru aukume hei rauemi whakatau māuiui.
eng_text: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: E whā tau ki muri ka tukuna tētahi raihana motuhake, koirā te raihana motuhake tuatahi o te ao i tukuna ki te mātai MRI.
eng_text: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: I te tau 1977, i whakaoti a Dr. Damadian i te hanganga o te matawai MRI "tinana-katoa" tuatahi, i tapaina e ia ko te "Indomitable".
eng_text: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Mā te whakawhitinga kōrero kāore i te wā tonu e āki ai te wā mō te whai whakaaro, me te urupare ki ētahi atu.
eng_text: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: E āhei ana ngā tauira ki te mahi ki tāna i pai ai, ki tāna i kī ai mō te āhua ki ngā pārongo tohutohu.
eng_text: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Hei tāpiritanga, he iti iho ngā here wā me te āheinga o te mahi i ngā hāora ā-mahi nekeneke. (Bremer, 1998)
eng_text: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Mā te whakamahi i te Ipurangi, me te Tukutuku-Ao-Whānui e āhei ai ngā ākonga ki te āhei atu ki ngā mōhiohio i ngā wā katoa.
eng_text: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Ka taea hoki e ngā ākonga te tuku pātai ki ngā kaiwhakaako ahakoa te wā o te rā, me te mōhio ka wawe te whakahoki, kaua ko te tatari tae atu ki te hui kanohi-ki-te-kanohi whai muri.
eng_text: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Kei te tukuna e te aronga postmodern ki te akoranga te wāteatanga mai i ngā whakaaro toka. Ehara i te mea kotahi anake te ara pai hei ako.
eng_text: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Waihoki, kāore tētahi mea pai hei ako.Ka tū mai te akoranga i te wheako i waenganui i te hunga e ako ana me te mātauranga e tukuna ana.
eng_text: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Kei te whakaaturia tēnei āhuatanga e tā mātou wheako ki ngā hōtaka pouaka whakaata ā-ako whakamahi-ake me te tuku mōhiohio.
eng_text: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Tokomaha o tātou ka tau ki te mātakitaki i tētahi hōtaka pouaka whakaata ka whakamōhio i a mātou ki tētahi hātepe, wheako rānei kore rawa tātou e whai wāhi, e whakahāngai rānei i taua mātauranga.
eng_text: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Kore rawa mātou e whakahou i tētahi waka, e hanga i tētahi puna torotī ki te iāri, te haere ki Peru hei mātai i ngā toenga o ngā whare tawhito, te whakahou rānei i te whare o te kiritata.
eng_text: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: i runga i te hononga tūhonohono opotiki weu ki a Ūropi me te āmiorangi tūhonohono anō hoki, e pai ana te honohono a Whenuakākāriki arā e 93% o te taupori e whai ana i te āheinga ipurangi.
eng_text: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Ko tōu hōtera, tō kaiwhakahaere rānei (mē e noho nei koe i te whare manuhiri, i tō kāinga tūmatawhāiti rānei) he hononga ipurangi kāore e kore, he rorohiko rānei kua hono ki te ipurangi, ā, ko ngā whakataunga katoa he kawhe ipurangi ōna, he wāhi rānei me te ipurangi tūmatawhānui.
eng_text: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: He pērā me runga nei, ahakoa e whakaaetia ana te kupu "Eskimo" ki roto o Amerika, e whakapono ana ētahi manene he kupu whakaparahako kē, koia pū ki roto o Kānata.
eng_text: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Ahakoa ka rangona pea te kupu e whakamahia ana e te Hunga Taketake o Whenuakākāriki, me ārai te hunga rāwaho i te whakamahi i taua kupu.
eng_text: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Ko te ingoa karanga o ngā iwi taketake o te Whenuakākāriki mō rātou anō ko te Inuit ki Kānata, ko te Kalaalleq (ngā Kalaallit), he tangata nō Whenuakākāriki, ki Whenuakākāriki.
eng_text: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Kāore i te tino mōhiotia te taihara me te kaikino whānui ki te hunga nō rāwaho ki Whenuakākāriki. Tae noa atu ki ngā tāone, kāore he "wāhi taumaha".
eng_text: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Ko te haurere makariri pea te mōrearea tūturu anake ka arohia e te hunga kāore i te whakaritea.
eng_text: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Ki te toro atu koe ki Whenua Kākāriki i ngā wā makariri (me whai whakaaro ake kia raki ake tō haere, ka makariri ake), he mea waiwai te kawe mai i ngā kākahu he rawaka te mahana.
eng_text: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: I runga i ngā rā tino roa ki te raumati ka raru pea kia rawaka te moe, ā, ka pāngia pea e ngā take hauora hāngai.
eng_text: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: I te raumati, me mataara hoki ki ngā naenae Nordic. Ahakoa kāore e tuku tahumaero, ka whakararu pea.
eng_text: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: He ahakoa te ōhanga o San Francisco e hono nei ki te take he wāhi tūruhi kounga o te ao, ko tana ōhanga kua tini.
eng_text: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Ko ngā rāngai mahi rahi rawa ko ngā ratonga ngaio, te kāwanatanga, te pūtea, te hokohoko, me te tāpoi.
eng_text: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Ko te tōaitanga o ngā puoro, ngā kiriata, ngā tuhinga me ngā ahurea rongonui i āwhina ai i te tāone me ana wāhi papai kia hau te rongo i te ao.
eng_text: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: Kua whakawhanaketia e San Francisco te hanganga tūruhi rahi whai i ngā tini hōtēra, whare kai, whare hui kounga anō hoki.
eng_text: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: Ko San Francisco hoki tētahi o ngā wāhi pai rawa o te motu mō ērā atu kai Āhia: arā te kai Kōria, Tairana, Īnia, Hapanihi anō hoki.
eng_text: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Ko te haere ki Walt Disney World tētahi haerenga tapu nui ki ngā tini whānau nō Amerika.
eng_text: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Ko te haerenga "māori" mai he rere ki te tāunga rererangi matua o Orlando, ka pahi ai ki te hōtera Disney kei te wāhi ake, ka noho ai ki reira mō te tahi wiki kāore e wehe i te takiwā o Disney, ka hoki ai ki te kāinga.
eng_text: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: He mutunga kore te rahi o ngā rerenga ka taea, ēngari ko tēnei tonu te tikanga o te nuinga o ngā tāngata i tā rātou kōrero mō te "haere ki Disney World".
eng_text: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: He maha ngā tīkiti e hokona tuihonotia ana mā ngā pae tukutuku hoko kairapu pērā i eBay, i Craiglist rānei he tīkiti piki-pāka tini-rangi kua whakamahia he wāhanga.
eng_text: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Ahakoa kei te whakamahia whānuitia tēnei mahi, kei te aukatia e Disney: he kore-whakawhiti ngā tīkiti.
eng_text: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Kei te hiahiatia tētahi whakaaetanga taiwhenua kia pūpahi ai ki raro i te tapa ki te Grand Canyon.
eng_text: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: E whakawhāititia ana ngā whakaaetanga hei whakahaumaru i te āpiti, ā, ka wātea mai hei te rangi tuatahi o te marama, e whā marama i mua i te marama tīmata.
eng_text: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Nā reira, ka wātea mai hei te rā 1 o Hānuere tētahi whakaaetanga tuawhenua mō ngā rā tīmata katoa i te marama o Mei.
eng_text: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: He wāhi kua roherohea mō ngā wāhi rongonui rawa, pērā me te wāhi hōpuni ki Bright Angel, kei te tahatika o Phantom Ranch, ka mūia e te tangata i te rangi kotahi.
eng_text: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: He pakupaku noa ngā whakaaetanga kua rāhuingia mō ngā tono hīkoi-mai i te āhuatanga ki te taenga mai tuatahi mai.
eng_text: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Ko te haere ki Awherika ki te Tonga mā runga motuka e kite ai te tangata i tōna ātaahua, me te kite hoki i ētahi wāhi i tua atu i ngā ara ka whāia e te tūruhi.
eng_text: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Ka taea tēnei ki tētahi waka noa ina āta whakamaheretia engari kei te tino tohua tētahi 4x4, ā, he maha ngā wāhi ka taea anake ki tētahi 4x4 he teitei te pūtake wīra.
eng_text: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: Kia mōhio hoki i te wā e whakamāhere ana he ahakoa he mauritau te Tonga o Awherika ehara i te mea he pēnei ngā whenua tata katoa.
eng_text: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Ka rerekē ngā hiahia pane uruwhenua me ngā utu mai i tētahi whenua ki tētahi atu, ā, ka pāngia koe e ai ki tō whenua tipu.
eng_text: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Kei ia motu hoki he ture ahurei e here ana i ngā rawa ohotata me noho ki roto i te waka.
eng_text: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Ko Victoria Falls tētahi tāone ki te wāhanga uru o Timuwawe, whakawhiti atu i te pae i Livingstone, Tāmipia, ā, tata ki Poriwana.
eng_text: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: E takoto ana te tāone ki kō tata atu ki te hīrere, ā, ko tērā te te whakamanea matua, heoi kei tēnei wāhi tūruhi rorotu ngā āhuatanga maha kia roa ake te noho a ngā waewae kai kapua, a te hunga tirotiro haere anō hoki.
eng_text: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: I te wā ua rawa o te tau (Noema tae atu ki Māehe), ka teitei ake te rōrahi wai, ā, ka wheriko ake ngā Wairere.
eng_text: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Ka mākū koe mēna koe ka whakawhiti i te piriti, ka hīkoi rānei i te huarahi kōpikopiko e tata ana ki te wairere.
eng_text: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Engari hoki, nā te nui o te wai i pērā ai, ā, ka rehurehu noa tō titiro atu ki ngā wairere- kei ngā wāhi katoa!
eng_text: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Te Toma o Tutankhamun (KV62). Ko KV62 te toma rongonui pea o ngā toma katoa ki te Taiororua, ko te wāhi i kitea i te tau 1922 e Howard Carter te nehunga kīngi tata houkura o te kīngi rangatahi.
eng_text: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Ki te whakatauritea ki te nuinga o ērā atu toma whare ariki, heoi anō, kāore te toma o Tutankhamun i te tino whai hua mō te toro atu, nā te mea he iti iho, he iti hoki te whakarākei.
eng_text: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Ko ērā e hiahia ana te kite i ngā tūkinotanga i pā ki te mami i te wā nukuhia atu ana mai i te kāwhena ka pāpouri mai i te mea ko te māhunga me ngā pakihiwi anake ka kitea.
eng_text: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Kāore ngā rawa mīharo o te toma i te noho tonu ki roto rā, engari kua haria ki te Egyptian Museum, ki Cairo.
eng_text: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Ko ngā manuhiri he iti te wā kua pai ake me i whai wāhi atu ki wāhi kē atu.
eng_text: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: 12 kiromita te tawhiti atu o Phnom Krom i Siem Reap. I hangaia te temepara i te pito o te rautau 9, i te wā o te arikitanga o Kīngi Yasovarman.
eng_text: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Ko te āhua hiawe o te temepara me te tirohanga o runga i te roto Tonle Sap e hiahiatia ai te piki i te puke.
eng_text: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Ka taea te whakakotahi māmā i tētahi toronga ki te wāhi tahi ki tētahi haerenga poti ki te roto.
eng_text: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Me whiwhi i te Pāhi Angkor kia tomo i te temepara, nōreira kaua e wareware kia haria mai tō uruwhenua i te haerenga ki Tonle Sap.
eng_text: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Ko Hiruharama te tāone matua o Iharaira, me te tāone nui rawa o reira, ahakoa kāore te nuinga o ērā atu whenua me te Kotahitanga o Ngā Iwi o te Ao e whakamana ana i a ia hei tāone matua o Iharaira.
eng_text: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: he hitori ataahua te taone onamata i ngā māunga Judean i roto i ngā mano tau.
eng_text: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: He tapu te tāone nui ki ngā hāhei kotahi-atua e toru - arā ko te Hūrae, te Karaitiana, me te Ihirama, ā, kei te noho hei pokapū ā-wairua, ā-hāhi, ā-ahurea anō hoki.
eng_text: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: I runga i te hiranga ā-hāhi o te tāone nui, inarā ko ngā tini wāhi o te rohe Old City, ko Hiruharama tētahi o ngā wāhi tūruhi matua ki Iharaira.
eng_text: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: He tini ngā wāhi hītori, ngā wāhi ahurea me ngā wāhi mātai whai toenga whare tangata ki Hiruhārama, tae atu hoki ki ngā pokapū hokohoko muramura e muia ana e te tangata, ngā whare kawhe me ngā whare kai.
eng_text: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Kei te here a Ekuatoa i ngā kainoho nō Kiupa kia riro i a rātou tētahi reta tono i mua i te uru atu ki Ekuatoa mā ngā tauranga waka rererangi ā-ao, i ngā wāhi kuhunga ripa.
eng_text: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Me whakature tēnei reta e te Ministry of Foreign Affairs ki Ekuatoa, me te ū hoki ki ētahi whakature.
eng_text: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Kua hoahoatia ēnei here hei tuku i tētahi rere whakaheke kua whakaritea i waenganui i ngā motu e rua.
eng_text: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Ko ngā kainoho o Kiupa e whai ana i ngā kāri kākāriki o Ngā Whenua Tōpū o Amerika me toro atu ki tētahi Ecuatorian Consulate kia whiwhi unutanga i tēnei here.
eng_text: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Me whai mana tō uruwhenua mō ngā marama e 6 neke atu i tō wā haerere. Me whai tūturutanga tō tīkiti kia mōhio ai ka mana mō te haerenga me te hokinga mai o tō haerenga.
eng_text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: He iti ake ngā haerenga mō ngā rōpu nui nei, nā reira mēnā e haere takitahi ana, takirua ana rānei, me whakahoahoa haere kia iti iho te utu ki ia tangata.
eng_text: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Heoi, ehara i te mea me aro koe ki tēnei kūraruraru, i te mea i te nuinga o te wā ka hurihuri ngā tūruhi kia whakakī i ngā motokā.
eng_text: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Ko te āhua nei he ara kia māminga i te tangata kia whakapono me nui ake te utu.
eng_text: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: I runga ake rā i te pito raki o Machu Picchu ko tēnei maunga paripari, he nui tāna tū hei ataata ki ngā whakaahua o ngā toenga whare.
eng_text: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: He whakapāhunu te āhua mai i raro, ā, he pikinga paripari, uaua hoki, engari ka taea e te nuinga o ngā tāngata āhua pakari te eke atu i te tata ki te 45 meneti.
eng_text: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Kei te whakatakotoria he arawhata kōhatu ki te nuinga o te ara, ā, ki ngā wāhi paripari ake he taura tīra hei puringa ā-ringa tautoko.
eng_text: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Ahakoa tēnā, ka korehāhā koe, me matāra hoki i ngā wāhi hōhonu, inā koa ka mākū ana, ka tere taka ai koe ki te raruraru.
eng_text: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: He ana paku rawa tata ki te tihi me puta, ā, he āhua pāpaka, he kōpē.
eng_text: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Ko te kite i ngā wāhi, i ngā kararehe o ngā Galapagos he pai rawa mā runga pōti, pērā i a Charles Darwin i te tau 835.
eng_text: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Neke atu i te 60 ngā waka nunui ka whakahipa i ngā wai o Galapago - ko te rahinga 8 ki te 100 ngā pāhihi.
eng_text: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Ko te nuinga o ngā tāngata ka whakarite i tō rātou wāhi noho i mua noa atu (i te nuinga o te wā e kī ana ngā poti i te wā o te kaupeka mātinitini).
eng_text: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Kia mataara ko te kaiwhakarite e whakarite ana i tō haerenga ko tētahi mātanga Galapagos me te mōhiohio pai o te whānuitanga o ngā kaipuke.
eng_text: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Mā konā e whakarite kia tūhonotia ō aronga, ō here hoki/rānei ki te kaipuke e tino hāngai ana ki ēnā.
eng_text: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: I mua i te taenga mai o te Paniora i te rautau 16, i raro a Chile ki te raki i te mana o Inca, ā, ko ngā māori o Araucanian (Mapuche) i noho atu ki te pokapū me te tonga o Chile.
eng_text: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Ko te Mapuche hoki tētahi o ngā rōpū taketake motuhake o Amerika, kāore i whakaurua katoatia ki raro i te mana kōrero-Pāniora tae noa atu ki te tū motuhake o Hiri.
eng_text: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: He ahakoa i tū motuhake a Chile i te tau 1810, (i roto i te wā o ngā pakanga Napoleonic i kore ai a Pāniora i whai kāwanatanga ā-motu whaitake mō ngā tau e rua), kāore tonu i whakatutuki te tino wikitoria ki ngā Pāniora tae rawa ki te tau 1818.
eng_text: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: He whenua Caribbean te Whenua Tominika (Reo Pāniora: Republica Dominicana) e mau ana ki te taha rāwhiti o te motu o Hispaniola, kei reira hoki a Haiti
eng_text: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: Atu i ngā takutai kirikiri mā me ngā pae maunga, ka kitea te taone nui tawhito nui o Ūropa ki Amerika, ināianei he wāhanga hoki nō Santo Domingo.
eng_text: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: I nohoia tuatahitia te motu e ngā Tainos me ngā Caribes. He hunga kōrero-Arawakan ngā Caribes, i tae atu tata ki te tau 10,000 BCE.
eng_text: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Ka taka ngā tau, whai muri mai i te taenga mai a te iwi Ūropi, i kitea te tāmatenga o te iwi Tainos i ngā mahi raupati a te iwi Pāniora.
eng_text: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: E ai ki Fray Bartolome de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) i waenganui i te tau 492 me te tau 1498 ka whakamatea tata ki te 100,000 F396Tainos e ngā toa Pāniora.
eng_text: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardīn de la Uniōn. I hangaia tēnei ātea hei whare ātea mō tētahi kaweneti o te 17 rautau, nā tēnei ko te temepara o San Diego te wharenui e tū tonu ana.
eng_text: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Ināianei ko tāna mahi ko te wāhi tūmatanui pokapū, ā, he nui ngā mahi kei te haere i te ao, i te pō.
eng_text: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: He maha ngā wharekai e karapoti ana i te māra, ā, i ngā ahiahi, i te ahiahi pō he konohete koreutu ka tino whakatūria mai i te whārau pokapū.
eng_text: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Huarahi o te Kihi). Ko ngā whakamahau e rua e wehea ana ki te 69 henimita noa iho ko te kāinga o tētahi pakiwaitara aroha tawhito.
eng_text: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Mō ngā kapa iti nei ka kōrerongia e ētahi tamariki te paki ki a koe.
eng_text: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Ko Bowen Island tētahi haerenga ā-rā rorotu, he haerenga mutunga wiki rānei e whakarato ana i te kōreti, te hīkoi maunga, ngā toa, ngā whare kai, aha atu.
eng_text: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Kei Howe Sound tēnei hapori houtupu ki tai tata ki Vancouver, ā, he māmā te tae atu mā ngā tēkehi wai e wehe ana i Granville Island kei te pokapū o te tāone o Vancouver.
eng_text: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Mō te hunga e pīkoko ana ki ngā mahi ō waho, he mea nui te wahi i te ara hīkoi, mai i te Moana ki te rangi
eng_text: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: He nui ngā utu ki Whistler (1.5 hāore te roa o te taraiwa i Vancouver) engari kei te mōhiotia whānuitia i runga i ngā Taumāhekeheke Hōtoke o te Ao i te tau 2010.
eng_text: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Kei Amerika ki te Raki te wāhi pai ki te reti hukapapa i ngā wā o te takurua, ā, hei ngā wā o te raumati tirohia ngā mahi eke paihikara.
eng_text: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Me rāhui ngā whakaaetanga i mua. Me whai whakaaetanga koe kia noho mō te pō ki Sirena.
eng_text: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Ko Sirena anake te teihana whare kaitiaki e tuku ana i te wharenoho rūma moe, te noho me ngā kai wera hei tāpiritanga ki te pūpahi. Kei La Leona, San Pedrillo me Los Patos te pūpahi anake, ā, kāore he ratonga kai.
eng_text: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Ka taea noatia te tango i ngā whakaaetanga ngāhere mai i te Teihana Ranger ki Puerto Jimēnez, heoi kāore e whakaaetia e rātou te kāri kererita.
eng_text: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Kāore te Park Service (MINAE) i te tuku i ngā whakaaetanga pāka i mua i te kotahi marama i mua i te rā ka tae pea mai.
eng_text: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: Kei te tuku a CafeNet El Sol i tētahi ratonga whakarite mō te utu o te $US30, te $10 rānei mō ngā tīkiti kotahi-rangi; kei tā rātou whārangi Corcovado ngā taipitopito.
eng_text: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Ko ngā Kuki Airini tētahi whenua motu e wātea ana te pāheko ki Aotearoa, kei Poronihia, ki waenga tonu i te South Pacific Ocean.
eng_text: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: He motumotu e 15 ngā motu e horapa ana i te 2.2 miriona km2 o te moana.
eng_text: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: E ōrite ana te wāhi wā ki tā hawaii, i tētahi wā kei te whakaarohia ngā motu hei "Hawaii ki raro".
eng_text: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Ahakoa he iti iho, kei te whakamaharatia ētahi manuhiri kaumātua ki Hawaaii i mua i te noho whenua karekau ngā hōtēra tūrihi rahi me ērā atu whakawhanaketanga.
eng_text: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Kāore i ngā Kuki Airani he tāone nui, engari 15 ōna motu. Ko ngā motu matua ko Rarotonga me Aitutaki.
eng_text: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Ki ngā whenua kua whakawhanaketia i tēnei wā, kua hīkina te tuku i ngā moenga me te parakuihi tino kounga ki tētahi momo toi.
eng_text: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Mō ngā B&B nui te kounga, ko te whakataetae matua ko ngā mea matua e rua: ngā rawa moenga me te parakuihi.
eng_text: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Me te mea hoki, i ngā wāhi kounga rawa atu kāore e kore ka kitea e tētahi ngā moenga tīno hirahira, ākuanei pea he koti riteta i mahia ā-ringatia, he moenga nō uki rānei.
eng_text: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Kei te parakuihi pea ko ngā kai reka o te wā nō te rohe, ko te kai motuhake o te hunga kāinga rānei.
eng_text: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Ko te wāhi nei pea he wāhi tawhito nei ngā whare me ōna nohoanga tawhito hoki, ko ngā papa e ātaahua ana, me tētahi puna kaukau.
eng_text: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: He manawa reka ki roto i te eke ki tō ake waka me te wehe atu ki tētahi haerenga huarahi roa i runga i tōna māmā.
eng_text: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Kua wāia kē pea koe ki te taraiwa i tōu ake waka, kaua ko ngā waka rahi ake, me te mōhio hoki ki ana here.
eng_text: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Mā te whakarite teneti ki runga i tētahi wāhi tūmatawhāiti, ki runga rānei i tētahi tāone ahakoa te nui, kāore e kore ka tae mai ngā titiro kikino.
eng_text: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: Hei whakarāpopoto, he ara pai rawa te whakamahi i tō waka mō te haere i tētahi haerenga huarahi engari he iti noa ngā wā he ara pai hei "pūpahi".
eng_text: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: Ka taea te hopuni ā-waka mehemea he wākena rahi, he SUV, he Sedan, he Station Wagon rānei tāu me ngā tūru ka taea te whakatakoto.
eng_text: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: He tukunga iho tō ētahi hōtēra mai i te tino wā o ngā ara tereina me ngā kaipuke moana tīma; i mua i te Pakanga Tuarua o te Ao, i te rautau 19, te tīmatanga o te rautau 20 rānei.
eng_text: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: Ko ngā hōtērā ēnei i noho ai te hunga whai rawa o te rā, ā, he nui ngā wā ka kai pai ka pāti i te pō.
eng_text: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: Ko ngā whitinga tawhito, ko te koretake o ngā taputapu hou, me tētahi momo ātaahuatanga i whai tirohanga mārihi ai ngā mea nei.
eng_text: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: Ahakoa motuhake ake nei, ka manaaki rātou i ētahi rangatira nō whenua kē i ētahi wā.
eng_text: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: Ka hiahia pea tētahi tangata waewae kai kapua he nui āna moni ki te rere i te ao, me te noho ki ngā tini o ēnei hōtera.
eng_text: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: He whakahaere e tūhonohono ai i ngā tūruhi me ngā tāngata whenua i roto i ngā tāone nui e haere nei rātou, tēnei mea te kōtuitui whakawhiti manaakitanga.
eng_text: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: I te nuinga o te wā ka hiahiatia anake te tūhono ki tētahi kōtuitui pērā te whakakī i tētahi puka tuihono; ahakoa kei te tuku, kei te hiahia rānei ētahi kōtuitui i te whakatūturutanga tāpiri.
eng_text: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: Ā, ka rewa ake ngā kaihautū e wātea ana mā te tā, mā te ipurangi hoki rānei, i ētahi wā he tuhinga arotake nā ētahi tāngata haerere kē atu.
eng_text: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: I whakatūria te Couchsurfing i te Kohitātea o te tau 2004 i muri i te hoko a te kaiwhakaite rorohiko a Casey Fenton i tētahi rerenga iti te utu ki Tiorangi engari kāore tōna wāhi noho.
eng_text: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: I tukuna atu e ia he īmera ki ngā ākonga o te whare wānanga ā-rohe, ā, i tini rawa atu ngā whakautu e tuku ana i te nohonga kore utu.
eng_text: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: Ko te kaupapa matua a ngā whare rangapū he kāinga kē mā te hunga rangatahi - ko te nuingā o te wā, 20 tau te pakeke o te manuhiri - engari ka kitea hoki te hunga kaumātua i ētahi wā.
eng_text: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: Me uaua te kite i ngā whānau whai tamariki, engari ka whakaaetia rātou e ētahi wharenoho ki ngā rūma tūmataiti.
eng_text: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: Ka noho te tāone nui o Beijing ki Haina hei tāone manaaki i Ngā Taumāhekeheke Hōtoke o te Ao hei te tau 2022, mā korā ka noho ia hei tāone nui tuatahi ki te manaaki i Ngā Taumāhekeheke o te Ao ki te raumati, ki te hōtoke anō hoki.
eng_text: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

text: Mā Beijing e noho hei hau kāinga mō ngā hui tuwhera, aukati anō hoki, me ngā mahi tio ki rō whare.
eng_text: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

text: Ko ngā huinga retireti kei te wāhi retireti Taizicheng ki Zhangjiakou, he āhua 220 km (140 mairo) mai i Beijing.
eng_text: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

text: Kei te nuinga o ngā whare karakia tētahi hui ā-Tau atu i te mutunga o te marama o Noema tae atu ki Waenga o Mei, ka rerekē ai i runga i te maramataka ā-tau o ia whare karakia.
eng_text: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

text: Ko te nuinga o ngā hui ahurei o te whare karakia ka whakanuitia hei wāhanga o te huringa tau o te temepara, o te rā whānau o te atua o reira, o tētahi atu wā nui rawa e hāngai ana ki taua temepara.
eng_text: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

text: He rawe katoa te whai wāhi atu ki ngā huinga temapara o Kerala, me te kitea hoki o ngā arewhana kua whakapaingia me ngā pūoro o te temepara me ngā ahurei kē atu hoki.
eng_text: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

text: Ko te Whakakitenga o te Ao (e kīia nei ko te World Exposition, ko te Expo noa rānei) he huihuinga nunui mō ngā mahi toi me ngā mahi mātauranga o te ao.
eng_text: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

text: Kei te whakaatu ngā whenua e whai wāhi ana i ngā whakaaturanga ā-toi, ā-mātauranga ki ngā whare ā-motu hei whakaatu i ngā take o te ao, i te ahurea, hītori rānei o tō rātou whenua.
eng_text: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

text: He hui whakahirahira ngā huihui Whakakitenga ahuru o te Ao, he whakaatu mai i ngā whakaaturanga putiputi, ngā mahi ahumāra me ngā kaupapa katoa e pā ana ki ngā huarākau.
eng_text: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

text: Ā-atiā nei, ka taea te whakahaere ia tau (me huri ngā hui i te ao), engari mō te whakaū i tēnei, ka kore e taea.
eng_text: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

text: Ka haere ēnei hui mō te toru ki te ono marama rānei, ā, ka whakatūria ki ngā wāhi kāore e iti iho i te 50 heketea.
eng_text: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

text: He nui ngā hanganga tewe rerekē kua whakamahia i roto i ngā tau. Ko te tewe aro whānui 35 mm (36 ki te 24 mm te whakaahua takahuri) te mea kei te tino whakamahia.
eng_text: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

text: I te nuinga o te wā he āhua māmā te whakahou mehemea ka pau, ā, ka āhua ōrite te ariari ki tētahi DSLF o nāianei.
eng_text: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

text: Ko ētahi o ngā kāmera kiriata-whānui ka whakamahi i te whakatakotoranga 6 mā te 6 cm, kia tika ake ko te 56 mā te 56 mm tōraro.
eng_text: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

text: I konei e tata ki te whā ngā whakareatanga te ariari i tēnā o te kiriata 35 mm (3136 mm2 ki te 864).
eng_text: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

text: Ko tētahi o ngā mahinga uaua mā te kaiwhakaahua ko te oranga mohoao, ā, me mau i ētahi āhuatanga pēnei i te kururaki, i te manawatā, i te wheakoranga me ngā taputapu papai.
eng_text: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

text: I ētahi wā kāore e tino whakanuitia ana te mau whakaahua ki ngā kararehe puihi, engari pērā i te mau whakaahua whānui, ka whakapuaki tētahi whakaahua i te kotahi mano kupu.
eng_text: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

text: Mēnā e whakaahua ana koe i ngā kararehe kei te taiao, me mau karaehe roa te kāmera, ahakoa ērā pērā ki ngā kāhui manu me ngā ngārara itiiti nei, me mau i ētahi atu karaehe.
eng_text: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

text: He uaua te kimi i ngā kararehe hou, ā, he ture hoki i ētahi wā mō te tango whakaahua mō ngā mahi tauhokohoko.
eng_text: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

text: Ko ngā kararehe pāwhara he whakamā, he ririhau rānei. Ko te taiao he makariri, he wera, he taraweti anō rānei.
eng_text: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

text: Neke atu i te 5,000 ngā momo reo, hei tāpiringa, neke atu i te 20 ngā iwi me te 50 miriona te nui o te hunga kōrero.
eng_text: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

text: I te nuinga o te wā he māma ake te mārama ki ngā kupu tuhituhi tēnā i ngā kupu kōrero. E pono pū ana tēnei mō te āhuatanga ki ngā wāhi noho, i te nuinga o te wā he uaua ki te whakahua tika.
eng_text: Written words are often easier to understand than spoken words, also. This is especially true of addresses, which are often difficult to pronounce intelligibly.

text: He nui ngā whenua katoa e matatau katoa ana ki te reo Ingarihi, ā, he nui atu anō ngā whenua kei reira te mātauranga here - inarā ki roto i ngā rangatahi.
eng_text: Many entire nations are completely fluent in English, and in even more you can expect a limited knowledge - especially among younger people.

text: Whai whakaarotia, mēnā e pai ana ki a koe, tētahi Mancunian, tētahi Bostonian, tētahi Jamaican me tētahi Syeneysider e noho ana ki tētahi tēpu e kai ana ki tētahi wharekai ki Toronto.
eng_text: Imagine, if you will, a Mancunian, Bostonian, Jamaican and Sydneysider sitting around a table having dinner at a restaurant in Toronto.

text: E whakangahau ngātahingia ana rātou ki ngā pakiwaitara mai i ō rātou wā kāinga, i roto anō hoki i ō rātou mita rerekē me ō rātou kupu ā-kaupapa.
eng_text: They're regaling each other with stories from their hometowns, told in their distinct accents and local argot.

text: I te nuinga o te wā ko te hoko kai ki ngā hokomahi te ara iti rawa te utu kia whangaia. Ki te kore ngā ara tunu kai, kua whāiti ngā kōwhiringa ki ngā kai kua whakaritea kētia.
eng_text: Buying food in supermarkets is usually the cheapest way to get fed. Without cooking opportunities, choices are however limited to ready-made food.

text: Kei te piki haere te whiwhi o ngā hokomaha i te kōwhiringa whānui ake o ngā kai kua whakaritea kētia. Kei ētahi he ngaruiti, he mea kē rānei hei whakamahana kai.
eng_text: Increasingly supermarkets are getting a more varied section of ready-made food. Some even provide a microwave oven or other means to heat food.

text: Ki ētahi whenua, momo toa rānei kei reira tētahi wharekai ki taua wāhi tonu i te itinga iho, he nui ngā wā he mea ōpaki me ngā utu pai.
eng_text: In some countries or types of stores there is at least one on-site restaurant, often a rather informal one with affordable prices.

text: Tāruatia tō kaupapa here me ngā taipitopito whakapā a tō kaiinihua, ā, me kawe hoki ki tō tinana.
eng_text: Make and carry copies of your policy and your insurer's contact details with you.

text: Me whakaatu atu e rātou te īmēra me ōna nama waea kia whiwhi tohutohu/whakamanatanga hoki mō te tuku kerēme.
eng_text: They need to show the insurer's e-mail address and international phone numbers for advice/authorizations and making claims.

text: Me whai i tētahi kape anō ki tāu haringa me te ipurangi (tukua he īmera ki a koe ake me te āpitihanga, ka penapenatia rānei ki te "kapua".
eng_text: Have another copy in your luggage and online (e-mail to yourself with attachment, or stored in the "cloud").

text: Ki te hāereere koe ki tētahi rorohiko pōnaha, paparorohiko rānei, whakaputua tētahi tāruatanga ki tōna pūmahara, ki tētahi kōpae rānei (ka taea atu horekau te ipurangi).
eng_text: If traveling with a laptop or tablet, store a copy in its memory or disc (accessible without the internet).

text: Me hoatu hoki he tārua kaupapa here/whakapā ki ngā hoa haere, ki ngā whanaunga, ngā hoa rānei ki te kāinga e pai ana ki te āwhina.
eng_text: Also give policy/contact copies to traveling companions and relatives or friends back home willing to help.

text: Kāore te Pihiringa (e mōhiotia ana hoki ko te Eoka) e tino riri, engari ka whawhai tonu mēnā ka taka ki te raru.
eng_text: Moose (also known as elk) aren't inherently aggressive, but will defend themselves if they perceive a threat.

text: Ki te kore te tangata e kite i te mōrearea pea o te muhi, ka whakatata rawa pea rātou, ka mōrearea.
eng_text: When people don't see moose as potentially dangerous, they may approach too closely and put themselves at risk.

text: Inumia ititia ngā inu waipiro. Ka rerekē te pā o te waipiro ki ia tangata, ā, he tino hira te mōhio ki tō tepenga.
eng_text: Drink alcoholic drinks with moderation. Alcohol affects everyone differently, and knowing your limit is very important.

text: Ka mate te ate i te inu waipiro, whāia mai hoki ka kāpō, ka mate. Ka raru kē atu mēnā ka inu waipiro kei waho i te ture.
eng_text: Possible long term health events from excessive drinking can include liver damage and even blindness and death. The potential danger is increased when consuming illegally produced alcohol.

text: Kei ngā waipiro turekore pea ngā momo para mōrearea tae atu ki te metanora, e kāpō ai, e hemo ai pea te tangata, ahakoa te iti o te kai.
eng_text: Illegal spirits can contain various dangerous impurities including methanol, which can cause blindness or death even in small doses.

text: ka iti ake te utu o ngā mōhiti ki whenua kē, ara hoki ko ngā ērā whenua e rawakore ana, ā, he iti ake te utu i ngā kaimahi.
eng_text: Eyeglasses can be cheaper in a foreign country, especially in low-income countries where labour costs are lower.

text: Whai whakaarotia te whiwhi i tētahi mātaitanga karu ki te kāinga, inarā e utua ana e te inihua, me te kawe mai i te whakahau rongoā kia whakakīia ki tētahi atu wāhi.
eng_text: Consider getting an eye exam at home, especially if insurance covers it, and bringing the prescription along to be filed elsewhere.

text: E rua pea ngā raru o ngā anga ingoa-parani nui te kounga e wātea ana ki ngā rohe pērā; ko ētahi he tāruatanga noa iho, ā ko ngā mea tūturu kua kawea mai ka nui ake pea te utu i te utu ki te kāinga.
eng_text: High-end brand-name frames available in such areas may have two problems; some may be knock-offs, and the real imported ones may be more expensive than at home.

text: Ko te kawhe tētahi o ngā kai rongonui ki te hoko huri noa i te ao, ka kitea hoki te huhua o ōna momo ki tō kāinga tonu.
eng_text: Coffee is one of the world's most traded commodities, and you can probably find many types in your home region.

text: Heoi anō, he maha ngā āhua rerekē o te inu kawhe huri noa i te ao he pai te whakamātau.
eng_text: Nevertheless, there are many distinctive ways of drinking coffee around the world that are worth experiencing.

text: Ko te haere āpiti (canyoneering rānei) e pā ana ki te heke ki te pūtake o te āpiti, ahakoa he maroke, e kī ana ki te wai rānei.
eng_text: Canyoning (or: canyoneering) is about going in a bottom of a canyon, which is either dry or full of water.

text: Ko te Canyon e whakakotahi ana i ngā āhuatanga o te kaukau, o te piki me te peke -- ēngari ehara i te mea me pakari rawa me nui tonu hoki ngā whakangungu (hei tauira, pēnei i te piki toka, i te ruku moana me te retireti maunga).
eng_text: Canyoning combines elements from swimming, climbing and jumping--but requires relatively little training or physical shape to get started (compared to rock climbing, scuba diving or alpine skiing, for example).

text: Ko te hīkoi ko tētahi mahi ki waho ko te tikanga ko te hīkoi ki ngā taiao māori, he nui ngā wā ki ngā ara hīkoi.
eng_text: Hiking is an outdoor activity which consists of walking in natural environments, often on hiking trails.

text: Ko te hīkoi rā ko ngā roanga iti iho i te te kotahi māero, tae atu ki ngā roanga roa ake ka taea te hīkoi i te rangi kotahi.
eng_text: Day hiking involves distances of less than a mile up to longer distances that can be covered in a single day.

text: Mō tētahi hīkoi ā-rā ki tētahi ara māmā kāore he tino whakaritenga e hiahiatia ana, ā, ka taea e tētahi tangata e āhua whiti ana te manawa reka i ērā.
eng_text: For a day hike along an easy trail little preparations are needed, and any moderately fit person can enjoy them.

text: Me nui ake pea te whakarite a tētahi whānau mēnā he tamariki itiiti ōnā, ēngari e tāea ana tētahi haerenga ā-waho mēnā he pēpi, he kōhungahunga rānei.
eng_text: Families with small children may need more preparations, but a day outdoors is easily possible even with babies and pre-school children.

text: I te ao,he tata ki t 200 ngā rōpū whakahaere omanga roa. Ko te nuinga ka tū motuhake.
eng_text: Internationally, there are nearly 200 running tour organizations. Most of them operate independently.

text: Ko te piki tūranga o The Global Running tours ka torotoro ki te huhua o ngā kaiomaoma i ngā whenua rahi e whā.
eng_text: The Global Running Tours successor, Go Running Tours networks dozens of sightrunning providers on four continents.

text: E tangata whenua ana ki roto o te omanga a Barcelona, a Running Tours Barcelona me te omanga o Copenhagen, a Running Tours Copenhagen, ka whai mai te Running Tours Prage i tū ki Prague tonu, me ētahi atu.
eng_text: With roots in Barcelona's Running Tours Barcelona and Copenhagen's Running Copenhagen, it was quickly joined by Running Tours Prague based in Prague and others.

text: He maha ngā mea me whai whakaaro e koe i mua i tō hāereere ki tētahi wāhi, i te wā e haere ana hoki.
eng_text: There are many things you have to take into consideration before and when you travel somewhere.

text: Ina hāereere koe, me mōhio koe ehara i te ōrite ngā āhuatanga ki ērā "ki te kāinga". Ko ngā whanonga, ngā ture, te kai, ngā waka, te noho, ngā taumata, te reo, aha atu anō, ka āhua rerekē i te wāhi e noho nā koe.
eng_text: When you travel, expect things not to be like they are "back home". Manners, laws, food, traffic, lodging, standards, language and so on will to some extent differ from where you live.

text: Koinei tētahi mea me maumahara koe i ngā wā katoa, kia kaupare ai i te pōuri, i te tāunu rānei ki ngā mahinga o tērā rohe.
eng_text: This is something you always need to keep in mind, to avoid disappointment or perhaps even distaste over local ways to do things.

text: Kua kitea he pokapū hāereere mai i te rautau 19. He kōwhiringa pai i te nuinga o te wā tētahi kaiwhakarite haerenga mō tētahi haerenga ka neke atu i te wheako o mua o tētahi tangata hāereere o te taiao, te ahurea, te reo, ngā whenua pohara rānei.
eng_text: Travel agencies have been around since the 19th century. A travel agent is usually a good option for a journey which extends beyond a traveller's previous experience of nature, culture, language or low-income countries.

text: He ahakoa e whakaae ana te nuinga o ngā tari ki te nuinga o ngā whakaritenga noa, arā ētahi kaiwhakarite ka hāngai pū noa ki ētahi momo haerenga, ki te rahi o te pūtea whakapau, ki ngā wāhi haere rānei.
eng_text: Although most agencies are willing to take on most regular bookings, many agents specialise in particular types of travel, budget ranges or destinations.

text: He pai ake te whakamahi i tētahi kaiwhakahaere haerenga mēnā he tini ana whakarite haerenga he rite nei ki āu.
eng_text: It can be better to use an agent who frequently books similar trips to yours.

text: Tirohia atu ki ngā haerenga e whakatairangatia ana e ngā kaiwhakahaere, mā te pae tukutuku, mā te matapihi rānei o te toa.
eng_text: Take a look at what trips the agent is promoting, whether on a website or in a shop window.

text: Ki te hiahia koe ki te kite i te ao ki te utu iti, i runga i te hiahia, te āhua o te noho, te wero rānei, he ara kia pēnā ai.
eng_text: If you want to see the world on the cheap, for necessity, lifestyle or challenge, there are some ways to do that.

text: Heoi anō, ka noho ki ngā rōpū e rua: Ka mahi i a koe e hāereere ana, tērā rānei me whakawhāiti koe i ō utu. E hāngai ana tēnei tuhinga ki te mea tuarua.
eng_text: Basically, they fall into two categories: Either work while you travel or try and limit your expenses. This article is focused on the latter.

text: Mō te hunga e pai ana ki te whakahere i te āhuru, i te wā, i te āhei ki te matapae hoki kia whakaheke i ngā utu tata atu ki te kore, tirohia te hāereere tahua pūtea itinga iho.
eng_text: For those willing to sacrifice comfort, time and predictability to push expenses down close to zero, see minimum budget travel.

text: Ko te whakapae kē, kāore te tangata karore e whānako, e aurara noa, e mahi kino, e pīnono haere, e takahi rānei i te manaakitanga a tētahi atu.
eng_text: The advice assumes that travellers do not steal, trespass, participate in the illegal market, beg, or otherwise exploit other people for their own gain.

text: Ko tētahi wāhi tiro kuhunga mai te tūnga tuatahi i te nuinga o te wā ka hekeheke i tētahi waka rererangi, kaipuke, waka atu anō rānei.
eng_text: An immigration checkpoint is usually the first stop when disembarking from a plane, a ship, or another vehicle.

text: Ka whakawātia ētahi tereina whakawhiti-rohe mā te tereina e haruru ana, ā, me whai tāutunga i tō ekenga ki tētahi o ēnei tereina.
eng_text: In some cross-border trains inspections are done on the running train and you should have valid ID with you when boarding one of those trains.

text: I ngā tereina-moe o ngā pō, ka kohia ngā uruwhenua e te kaitaki tereina kia kore ai koe e whakahōhātia nōu e moe ana.
eng_text: On night sleeper trains, passports may be collected by the conductor so that you do not have your sleep interrupted.

text: He hiahia tāpiri te rēhitatanga mō te hātepe pane uruwhenua. Ki ētahi motu, me rēhita koe i tō noho ki reira, me te wāhitau e noho ana koe ki ngā mana ki reira.
eng_text: Registration is an additional requirement for the visa process. In some countries, you must register your presence and address where you are staying with the local authorities.

text: Akuanei pea me whakakī te pepa nei me ngā pirihimana o te rohe, i tētahi toronga atu rānei ki te tari manene.
eng_text: This might require filling out a form with the local police or a visit to the immigration offices.

text: Ki ngā tini whenua me tētahi ture pērā, ka whakarite ngā hōtēra ā-rohe i te rēhitatanga (me mātua tono atu).
eng_text: In many countries with such a law, local hotels will handle the registration (make sure to ask).

text: I ētahi atu wā, ko te hunga ō waho i ngā nohoanga tūruhi anake me rēhita. Heoi, mā tēnei e kore ai e tīno mārama ki te ture, nā reira me mōhio i mua noa atu.
eng_text: In other cases, only those staying outside of tourist accommodations need to register.  However, this makes the law much more obscure, so find out beforehand.

text: Ko te waihanga whare ko te hanganga me te tārai i ngā whare. Ko te hoahoanga o tētahi wāhi he wāhi e rata ana ki te hunga tūruhi.
eng_text: Architecture is concerned with the design and construction of buildings. The architecture of a place is often a tourist attraction in its own right.

text: He maha ngā wharenui he ātaahua te tirohanga atu, ā, he ātaahua hoki te tirohanga mai i te tihi o tētahi whare teitei, mai i tētahi matapihi he koi te whakatakoto he rerehua te tirotiro atu.
eng_text: Many buildings are quite beautiful to look at and the view from a tall building or from a cleverly-positioned window can be a beauty to behold.

text: He hononga nui tō te hoahoanga ki ngā mahinga kē atu pēnei i te whakahoanga tāone, i te pūhanga metarahi, i te toi whakarākei, i ngā toi rōwhare me te hoahoa horanuku hoki.
eng_text: Architecture overlaps considerably with other fields including urban planning, civil engineering, decorative arts, interior design and landscape design.

text: I te mea o te noho ki rāhaki a te tokomaha o ngā Pueblo, e kore koe e kite i te nui o te whakangahau ā-pō kia haere rā anō ki Albuquerque, ki Santa Fe rānei.
eng_text: Given how remote many of the pueblos are, you won't be able to find a significant amount of nightlife without traveling to Albuquerque or Santa Fe.

text: Heoi anō, tata ki te katoa o ngā whare petipeti kua rārangihia ki runga ake e whakarato ana i ngā inu, ā, kei te tō mai ētahi o rātou i te whakangahau ingoa-parani (inarā ko ngā mea rahi e tino tata ana ki Albuquerque me Santa Fe).
eng_text: However, nearly all of the casinos listed above serve drinks, and several of them bring in name-brand entertainment (primarily the large ones immediately surrounding Albuquerque and Santa Fe).

text: Kia tūpato: kāore ngā pāpara kauta o ngā tāone iti ki konei i te wāhi pai i ngā wā katoa mō te manuhiri nō waho i te takiwā.
eng_text: Beware: small-town bars here are not always good places for the out-of-state visitor to hang out.

text: Ko tētahi take, he tini ngā raruraru taraiwa haurangi o te raki o te New Mexico, ā, ko te tōpūtanga o ngā kaitaraiwa haurangi he teitei pātata ki ngā pāpara o ngā tāone iti.
eng_text: For one thing, northern New Mexico has significant problems with drunk driving, and the concentration of intoxicated drivers is high close to small-town bars.

text: Ko ngā muraiti me ngā tuhinga anuanu hoki e mōhiotia ana hei karawhiti.
eng_text: Unwanted murals or scribble is known as graffiti.

text: Ahakoa he tawhito te āhua, ko te nuinga e mea ana nā te rangatahi ēnei mahi, he āhuatanga kikino, he tūkino i ngā taputapu mā te peita rehurehu.
eng_text: While it's far from a modern phenomenon, most people probably associate it with youth vandalizing public and private property using spray paint.

text: Heoi, i ēnei rangi nei he kaituhituhi pakitara whakapūmau, he hinonga tuhituhi pakitara "ture" tika. Ko ngā tuhinga pakitara pēnei e mōhiotia ana hei mahi toi, ehara noa i ngā tuhituhi takahi ture.
eng_text: However, nowadays there are established graffiti artists, graffiti events and "legal" walls. Graffiti paintings in this context often resemble artworks rather than illegible tags.

text: He pukenga kei roto i te whiu taipere e hiahiatia nei e te hunga tūruhi.
eng_text: Boomerang throwing is a popular skill that many tourists want to acquire.

text: Ki te hiahia koe ki te ako ki te whiu i tētahi pumarangi ka hokihoki mai ki tō ringa, whakaritea he pumarangi tāu e tika ana mō te hokihoki.
eng_text: If you want to learn throwing a boomerang that comes back to your hand, make sure you have a suitable boomerang for returning.

text: Ko te nuinga o ngā pumarangi kei Ahitereiria he kore auraki mai. He pai ake kia kauaka ngā torekaihuruhuru e whiu i roto i te hau
eng_text: Most boomerangs available in Australia are in fact non-returning. It is best for beginners to not try throwing in windy

text: Kei te tunua tētahi Kai Hāngī ki tētahi rua wera ki te papa.
eng_text: A Hangi Meal is cooked in a hot pit in the ground.

text: Ka whakamahanatia te rua ki ngā kōhatu wera mai i tētahi ahi, tērā rānei ki ētahi wāhi ka wera noa mai ngā wāhi o te whenua i te mahana ngāwhā.
eng_text: The pit is either heated with hot stones from a fire, or in some places geothermal heat makes areas of ground naturally hot.

text: He nui te whakamahi i te hāngī hei tunu i tētahi kai tunu tūturu.
eng_text: The hangi is often used to cook a traditional roast style dinner.

text: Kei ētahi wāhi ki Rotorua he hāngī ngāwhā, ā, ka taea ētahi atu hāngī te kai ki Ōtautahi, ki Pōneke, ki wāhi kē atu anō.
eng_text: Several places in Rotorua offer geothermal hangi, while other hangi can be sampled in Christchurch, Wellington and elsewhere.

text: Kei MetroRail ngā taumata e rua ki ngā tereina kaieke ki roto i Cape Town, huri noa hoki: ko MetroPlus (ka kīia hoki ko Taumata Tuatahi), me Metro (e kīia ana ko Taumata Tuatoru).
eng_text: MetroRail has two classes on commuter trains in and around Cape Town: MetroPlus (also called First Class) and Metro (called Third Class).

text: He hāneanea, ā, kāore hoki e tino nui te tāngata ki MetroPlus, engari he nui ake te utu. Heoi, he iti tonu ngā utu o ngā tīkiti ki ērā atu utu kei Ūropi.
eng_text: MetroPlus is more comfortable and less crowded but slightly more expensive, though still cheaper than normal metro tickets in Europe.

text: Katoa ngā tereina, nā MetroPlus me Metro; Ko ngā tereina MetroPlus kei te pito o te tereina e tata ana ki Cape Town.
eng_text: Every train has both MetroPlus and Metro coaches; the MetroPlus coaches are always on the end of the train nearest Cape Town.

text: Te kawe mō ētahi atu - Kaua rawa e waiho i ō pēke kei waho i tō tirohanga, inarā e whakawhiti ana koe i ngā pae o whenua kē.
eng_text: Carrying for others - Never let your bags out of your sight, especially when you are crossing international borders.

text: Ka whakamahia pea koe hei kaikawe tarukino ahakoa tō kore mōhio, mā korā koe e tau ki te tino raru.
eng_text: You could find yourself being used as a drug carrier without your knowledge, which will land you in a great deal of trouble.

text: Kei roto i tēnei me tatari ki te rārangi, e taea ana te whakamahi i ngā kurī rapu tarukino i te wā e hiahiatia ana horekau te whaki atu i mua.
eng_text: This includes waiting in line, as drug-sniffing dogs could be used at any time without notice.

text: Kei ētahi motu he whiunga tino taumaha rawa ahakoa he taihara wā tuatahi; kei roto i ēnei ko ngā whiunga noho whare herehere mō te neke atu i te 10 tau, te mate rānei.
eng_text: Some countries have exceedingly draconian punishments even for first time offenses; these can include prison sentences of over 10 years or death.

text: He aronga tāhei ngā pēke kāore i te tiakina, ā, ka tō mai hoki pea te tirohanga o ngā mana e mataara ana ki ngā whakatuma pōmu.
eng_text: Unattended bags are a target for theft and can also attract attention from authorities wary of bomb threats.

text: Ki te kāinga, i runga i tēnei huranga ki ngā moroiti o tērā wāhi, ākene pea he ārai mate kē tāu ki ēnā.
eng_text: At home, due to this constant exposure to the local germs, odds are very high that you're already immune to them.

text: Heoi anō ki ētahi atu wāhi o te ao, kei reira ngā kīrehe e tauhou ana ki a koe, ka nui ake te tupono ka raru koe.
eng_text: But in other parts of the world, where the bacteriological fauna are new to you, you're far more likely to run into problems.

text: Me te mea hoki, ki ngā āhuarangi mahana ake ka tere ake te tupu a te huakita, ka roa hoki ake tana ora ki waho atu i te tinana.
eng_text: Also, in warmer climates bacteria both grow more quickly and survive longer outside the body.

text: Ko ngā whiu a Delhi Belly, ko te kanga a Parao, ko te rānaki a Montezuma, me ō rātou hoa tinitini.
eng_text: Thus the scourges of Delhi Belly, the Pharaoh's Curse, Montezuma's Revenge, and their many friends.

text: Ka pērā i ngā mate hā ki ngā āhuarangi makariri ake, he āhua noa ngā raru kōpiro ki ngā āhuarangi wera, ā, i te nuinga o te wā he mātua tiotio engari ehara i te tino mōrearea.
eng_text: As with respiratory problems in colder climates, intestinal problems in hot climates are fairly common and in most cases are distinctly annoying but not really dangerous.

text: Mēnā e haere ana koe i tētahi whenua whanake mō te wā tuatahi - ki tētahi wāhanga hou rānei o te ao - kaua e whakahāwea ki ngā pitomata ahurea.
eng_text: If traveling in a developing country for the first time – or in a new part of the world – don't underestimate the potential culture shock.

text: He maha ngā tāngata haereere kua ohorere i ngā whanaketanga ki te ao haereere, e iti nei ngā rerekētanga ahurea e hahū ake ana.
eng_text: Many a stable, capable traveler has been overcome by the newness of developing world travel, where many little cultural adjustments can add up quickly.

text: Inā hoki i te tīmatanga, whāia ngā hōtēra whai kounga, ngā kai pai, me ngā ratonga pai kia pai ai tō whakamauru ake.
eng_text: Especially in your initial days, consider splurging on Western-style and -quality hotels, food, and services to help acclimatize.

text: Kaua e moe ki runga mēterehi ki te kore koe e mōhio ki taua whenua.
eng_text: Do not sleep on a mattress or pad on the ground in areas where you do not know the local fauna.

text: Mēnā ka moe tēneti koe, mauria mai tētahi moenga pēpi tēneti, tētahi moenga whakawerewere rānei kia noho wehe koe i ngā nākahi, i ngā hikutimo, i ngā aha atu.
eng_text: If you are going to camp out, bring a camp cot or hammock to keep you away from snakes, scorpions and such.

text: Whakakīia tōu whare ki tētahi kawhe mōmona i te ata, ki te tī kamomira whakatā i te pō.
eng_text: Fill your home with a rich coffee in the morning and some relaxing chamomile tea at night.

text: I te wā e hararei ana koe ki te kāinga, kei a koe te wā hei whakareka i a koe, me te whakarite i tētahi mea motuhake mō ētahi atu meneti anō.
eng_text: When you're on a staycation, you have the time to treat yourself and take a few extra minutes to brew up something special.

text: Mehemea he waewae kai kapua koe, tīkina te rākau kia whakaranu, kia kōmitimiti rānei i ētahi ranunga:
eng_text: If you're feeling more adventurous, take the opportunity to juice or blend up some smoothies:

text: ka kite pea koe i tētahi inu māmā ka taea te whakarite mā te parakuihi ina kua hoki atu koe ki āu mahi o ia rā.
eng_text: maybe you'll discover a simple beverage that you can make for breakfast when you're back to your daily routine.

text: Kite noho koe i tētahi tāone he ahurea inuinu, me haere ki ngā pāpara kāuta ki ngā pāpara rānei kei ngā whare tata ehara i te wāhi haerenga māu.
eng_text: If you live in a city with a varied drinking culture, go to bars or pubs in neighborhoods you don't frequent.

text: Mō te hunga kāore i te waia ki ngā kupu rongoā, he motuhake ngā tikanga o ngā kupu infectious me te contagious.
eng_text: For those unfamiliar with medical jargon, the words infectious and contagious have distinct meanings.

text: Ko te mate hōrapa tētahi tahumaero nā tētahi tukumate te take, pēnei i te huaketo, i te ngārara, i te hekaheka, i ētahi atu pirinoa rānei.
eng_text: An infectious disease is one that is caused by a pathogen, such as a virus, bacterium, fungus or other parasites.

text: kua pāngia e tēnei urutā, he pātata rawa hoki nō te noho ki tētahi tangata.
eng_text: A contagious disease is a disease which is easily transmitted by being in the vicinity of an infected person.

text: He tini ngā kāwanatanga e here ana i ngā manuhiri e uru mai ana, i ngā kainoho e wehe ana, i ō rātou whenua te whai rongoā ārai mate mō ētahi tahumaero.
eng_text: Many governments require visitors entering, or residents leaving, their countries to be vaccinated for a range of diseases.

text: Ka whirinaki pea ēnei here ki ngā whenua kua torohia e tētahi kaihāereere, kei te takune rānei kia torohia.
eng_text: These requirements may often depend on what countries a traveller has visited or intends to visit.

text: Ko tētahi o ngā āhuatanga pai o Charlotte, ki North Carolina, ko tana huhua o ngā kōwhiringa tino kounga mā ngā whānau.
eng_text: One of strong points of Charlotte, North Carolina, is that it has an abundance of high-quality options for families.

text: Ko ngā kainoho mai i wāhi kē atu i te nuinga o te wā ko te whanaungatanga te take nui e hūnuku ai ki reira, ā, he tini ngā wā e whakatau ai ngā tūruhi he māmā te taone nei mō te nohonoho me ō tamariki.
eng_text: Residents from other areas often cite family-friendliness as a primary reason for moving there, and visitors often find the city easy to enjoy with children around.

text: I te 20 tau kua pahure ake, ko te nui o ngā kōwhiringa pai mā te tamariki ki Uptown Charlotte kua tipu rawa atu nei.
eng_text: In the past 20 years, the amount of child-friendly options in Uptown Charlotte has grown exponentially.

text: Kāore ngā whānau i Charlotte i te tino whakamahi tākihi, ahakoa ka whai take i ētahi wā.
eng_text: Taxis are not generally used by families in Charlotte, though they can be of some use in certain circumstances.

text: He utu āpiti mō te whai i te nui ake i te 2 pāhihi, nō reira ka nui pea te utu mō tēnei kōwhiringa i te mea waiwai.
eng_text: There is a surcharge for having more than 2 passengers, so this option might be more expensive than necessary.

text: Ko Te Kōpakatanga ki te Tonga te wāhi makariri rawa ki te Ao, ā, e karapoti ana i Te Pito Whakarunga o te Ao.
eng_text: Antarctica is the coldest place on Earth, and surrounds the South Pole.

text: He nui te utu mō ngā toronga tūruhi, me tino pakari te tinana, ā, ka taea anake te tū ki te raumati atu i te marama o Nōema ki Pēpuere, ā, kua mātua whakawhāititia ki te Peninsula, ngā Islands me te Ross Sea.
eng_text: Tourist visits are costly, demand physical fitness, can only take place in summer Nov-Feb, and are largely limited to the Peninsula, Islands and Ross Sea.

text: He ruarua mano ngā kaimahi ka noho ki konei i te raumati ki ngā whare e whā taihana, ko te nuinga kei ērā wāhi; tokoiti ka noho i te wā o te takurua.
eng_text: A couple of thousand staff live here in summer in some four dozen bases mostly in those areas; a small number stay over winter.

text: He whenua mōwai te taiwhenua o Antarctica, e kapia ana e te huka, 2-3 kiromita te whānui.
eng_text: Inland Antarctica is a desolate plateau covered by 2-3 km of ice.

text: Ka haere tuawhenua ngā haerenga rere motuhake i ētahi wā ruarua, mō te eke maunga, te tae atu rānei ki te Tōpito o te Ao, kei reira tētahi wāhi noho nui.
eng_text: Occasional specialist air tours go inland, for mountaineering or to reach the Pole, which has a large base.

text: Ko te whakawhitinga Pou Tonga (ara matua rānei) he huarahi 1600 km mai i te teihana McMurdo o te Moana Ross ki te Pou.
eng_text: The South Pole Traverse (or Highway) is a 1600 km trail from McMurdo Station on the Ross Sea to the Pole.

text: He hukapapa kīato, ā, kua whakakīia, kua tohua ki te haki ngā āpiti. Ka taea anake ngā tarakihana motuhake te haere ki reira, e tō ana i ngā panuku ki te kora, ki ngā ratonga hoki.
eng_text: It's compacted snow with crevasses filled in and marked by flags. It can only be traveled by specialized tractors, hauling sleds with fuel and supplies.

text: Kāore ēnei i te tino kakama nō reira me roa te kōtiutiu o te ara ki ngā Transantarctic Mountains kia eke ki te mānia.
eng_text: These aren't very nimble so the trail has to take a long swerve around the Transantarctic Mountains to come onto the plateau.

text: Ko te take matua o ngā aituā ki te hōtoke ko ngā huarahi pāremoremo, ko ngā ara hīkoi (ara taha huarahi), ā, inarā ko ngā arawhata.
eng_text: The most common cause for accidents in winter is slippery roads, pavements (sidewalks) and especially steps.

text: I te itinga iho, me mau he hū whai raparapa tika. He tino pāremoremo ngā hū raumati ki te tio, ki te hukapapa, ā, he takarepa hoki ētahi pūtu hōtoke.
eng_text: At a minimum, you need footwear with suitable soles. Summer shoes are usually very slippery on ice and snow, even some winter boots are deficient.

text: Me rawaka te hōhonu o te tauira, 5 mm (1/5 inihi) neke atu rānei, ā, me rawaka te ngohe o te matū ki ngā paemahana makariri.
eng_text: The pattern should be deep enough, 5 mm (1/5 inch) or more, and the material soft enough in cold temperatures.

text: He whao ā ētahi pūtu, ā, he taputapu whao tāpiri mō ngā āhuatanga pāremoremo, e tika ana mō te nuinga o ngā hū, ngā pūtu rānei, mō ngā rekereke, ngā rekereke me ngā kapukapu rānei.
eng_text: Some boots have studs and there is studded add-on equipment for slippery conditions, suitable for most shoes and boots, for the heels or heels and sole.

text: Me pāpaku, me whānui ngā rekereke. He rite tonu te ruirui i te oneone, i te matakirikiri, i te tote (konopūmā pūhaumāota) ki ngā huarahi, ki ngā ara rānei hei whakapai ake i te pupuri.
eng_text: Heels should be low and wide. Sand, gravel or salt (calcium chloride) is often scattered on roads or paths to improve traction.

text: Ehara i te rerekē ngā horonga huka; ka taea anake e ngā paripari te pupuri i ētahi hukapapa, ā, ka makere ngā rōrahi hau hei horonga huka.
eng_text: Avalanches are not an abnormality; steep slopes can hold only so much slow, and the excess volumes will come down as avalanches.

text: Ko te raru ko te piri o te hukapapa, nō reira me turupana kia heke mai, ā, ko te hukapapa e heke ana pea te mahi turupana mō te toenga.
eng_text: The problem is that snow is sticky, so it needs some triggering to come down, and some snow coming down can be the triggering event for the rest.

text: I ētahi wā ko te kaupapa e whakaohooho ai i ngā mahinga tirikini ko te rā e whakamahana nei i te hukarere, i ētahi wā ētahi anō hukarere, ētahi wā ko ētahi kē atu mahinga māori, ētahi wā te tangata.
eng_text: Sometimes the original trigging event is the sun warming the snow, sometimes some more snowfall, sometimes other natural events, often a human.

text: He pou āwhiowhio te āwhā, he māmā te pūroto ka horomi noa i te hau ō roto, ō waho hoki.
eng_text: A tornado is a spinning column of very low-pressure air, which sucks the surrounding air inward and upward.

text: Ka puta ngā hau kaha (100-200 mairo/haora te nuinga) ā, e āhei ana te hiki i ngā mea nui ki te rangi, e kawea ana i te nekehanga o te awhiowhio.
eng_text: They generate high winds (often 100-200 miles/hour) and can lift heavy objects into the air, carrying them as the tornado moves.

text: I te tīmatanga, he kauhau noa e puea ake ana, nā wai ka āwhiowhio ka tae ana ki te whenua.
eng_text: They begin as funnels descending from storm clouds, and become "tornadoes" when they touch the ground.

text: Ko ngā kaituku whaiaro VPN (virtual private network) tētahi ara pai rawa o te huri āwhio i te rāhui whakaaturanga tōrangapū me te IP-geofiltering ahumahi.
